title: [guides] Unavailable answers need a better presentation
description:
DrTorte, 2026-09-30: 'Perhaps there are better ways of showing the options that are not available.'

The engine already works out which answers would empty a part - resolve returns an 'unavailable' list per question, with a 'because' map naming the role that would come back empty. So the information is there and correct; this is about how it is shown.

Worth deciding what the page should do with it, because there are three defensible answers and they read very differently to a patron:

- grey the option out and say why on hover or focus ('no 1 inch wall base')
- hide it entirely, so the wizard only ever offers buildable answers
- show it, let it be picked, and explain the result on the parts side

Hiding is tempting and probably wrong: the option existing tells you the catalog has that idea in it, and silently dropping it makes the guide look thinner than the catalog is. Greying with a reason is likely the honest middle.

Context that makes this matter more than it looks: some combinations really are dead. separate-wall at 1x1 has no wall base for any texture (openforge_catalog-f8l), and the two building-facade textures are dead in 18 of 24 method-and-size combinations (openforge_catalog-sq5). Until those are fixed, presentation is what stands between a patron and a blank parts list.

title: Guides: _blame's hypothetical ordering is only observable when the dead answer is a step
description:
From round 7 of PR #241 (general-reviewer's "watch next round" note, and test-coverage-reviewer F7 / thread 4115860072).

_blame builds its hypothetical as _with_defaults(document, {**without, question: value}) -- the candidate answer goes in BEFORE the defaults are derived, because _with_defaults walks questions in order and a conditional default branches on the answers so far. Deriving first and overlaying afterwards would compute a later question's default for the branch being left.

The fix is in (round 7). It is NOT pinned by a test, and the reason is structural rather than laziness: the ordering can only change the outcome when the dead answer being explained is a STEP whose value gates a conditional default below it. Every blame assertion in the suite targets a refinement, where the override is a no-op. The obvious constructions fail for an unrelated reason: refinements are held back until every step is explicitly answered (resolve returns an empty refinements list while any step is unanswered), so a fixture with an unanswered step produces no because-entry for a texture at all.

What a real test needs: a dead answer on a STEP option, a later step whose default is a clause list branching on that step, and a catalog where the two branches differ. Probably easier at the resolve() level in tests/test_guides_resolve.py than through the route.

Mutation that currently survives: derive the defaults from `without` and overlay the candidate afterwards -- 123 guide tests stay green.

title: [infra] A bare-path link on openforge.tools 302s to /current/ and 404s, dropping the query
description:
Any internal link without a trailing slash is fatal in production, and it leaks the deploy prefix on the way.

Probed live, read-only:

    https://openforge.tools/admin        -> 302 -> https://openforge.tools/current/admin/ -> 404
    https://openforge.tools/admin?x=1    -> 302 -> https://openforge.tools/current/admin/ -> 404   (query dropped)
    https://openforge.tools/admin/?x=1   -> 200

Two separate faults in one redirect:

1. The `Location` carries `/current/`, which is the internal S3 prefix the deploy promotes into — CloudFront serves `current/` as the root, so the prefix should never appear in a URL a browser sees. Following it 404s.
2. The query string is discarded. Even if the path resolved, `?guide=wall` or any deep link would arrive empty.

The frontend is built with `trailingSlash: true` and `output: "export"`, so every route is `<name>/index.html` and the slash-less form always needs this redirect. The repo's own internal links happen to be `/` and `/?…` today, which is why nobody has hit it.

Found by frontend-conventions-reviewer in round 1 of PR #246 while checking a link I had written as `/guides?guide=<key>` — it would have been dead in production. The link is fixed in that PR; this ticket is the underlying redirect, which is independent of it and pre-existing.

Lives in `openforge-infra-frontend` (the CloudFront distribution and the S3 website endpoint), not this repo. Worth fixing before anything links to a bare path again, because the failure is invisible in `npm run dev` — Next 308s and preserves the query there, so it only appears in production.

title: [dropbox] Curved wall bases have no 'wall' in their names, so nothing can find them
description:
The 244 files under tiles/bases/separate_wall/curved_walls carry no "wall" in their form, so they parse to shape|base plus a bare shape|wall (from the curved_walls directory) and never get shape|base|wall. Anything asking for a wall base — the wall guide does — cannot see them.

This is the same fault fixed under primary_walls on 2026-09-21, where 128 files named "plain#base.A..." were renamed to "plain#base+wall.A...". Deliberately not fixed here at the same time, because unlike primary_walls there is no correctly-named file in this folder to copy: all 244 are consistent with each other, so applying the primary_walls convention would be inventing one rather than following one.

What is there now, by texture folder:

  base#curved%dungeon_stone   102
  base#curved%plain            76
  base#curved%wood             40
  base#curved%cut-stone        26

Forms in use: base+curved, base+curved+concave, base+curved+convex, base+mirror+curved, and +low variants of the concave and convex ones.

The presumed fix, to be confirmed rather than assumed:

- base+curved+concave  ->  base+wall+curved+concave, and so on for each form
- base+mirror+curved   ->  base+wall+curved with "+mirror" moved into the size, which is where primary_walls puts it: aztlan#base+wall.BA+mirror.dragonlock,magnetic+flex.stl

Watch out for one thing that makes this less mechanical than it looks: "base+curved" is also the correct name in tiles/bases/separate_wall/curved_floors, where 23 files use it for curved *floor* bases and legitimately have no wall. The same form is right in one folder and wrong in another, so any rename has to be scoped to curved_walls rather than matched on the filename alone.

Each STL has a matching -thumb.png that has to be renamed with it, or the thumbnail is orphaned. The primary_walls rename moved 128 of each.

Devon: revisit when we do the curved wall wizard.

title: setup.py packages only the top-level openforge package, so a non-editable install is empty
description:
`setup.py` says `packages=["openforge"]`, which does not recurse. A built wheel contains `openforge/__init__.py` plus three bin scripts — about 4.4 KB — against 75 `.py` files under `openforge/`. `package_data` keys are paths rather than dotted package names, so the fixtures miss too.

Nothing has failed because nothing depends on the install: CI uses `pip install -e .` (path-based, so it works), and `Dockerfile.api.deploy` does `COPY openforge ./openforge` with `LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT=/var/task` ahead of site-packages, so the image shadows the broken install with the real tree. `RUN python setup.py install` in that Dockerfile is doing nothing useful.

Why it is worth fixing rather than leaving: it is a trap with a quiet failure mode. `get_schema_versions()` enumerates migrations with `os.listdir(os.path.dirname(__file__))`, so any packaging that does not lay the modules out as files on disk yields an empty list — and before PR #248 added a head assertion, that returned `{"ok": true, "applied": []}` and passed the deploy gate. A zipped or properly-packaged install would silently migrate nothing.

Fix: `find_packages(include=["openforge*"])` and dotted `package_data` keys, then drop the `setup.py install` line from the Dockerfile or keep it and remove the `COPY` — one or the other, not both.

Found by the serverless-architecture pass on PR #248, which built the wheel to check.
close_reason: Duplicate of openforge_catalog-li2, which predates it. Evidence merged there and that ticket raised to P2. I filed this without searching existing beads first.

title: Blame a recommended answer, not just an answered one
description:
Blame currently names only questions the person actually answered. A question
sitting on its recommendation can never be blamed, because the counterfactual
is derived from what was sent: removing a key the person never sent leaves the
map unchanged, so the hypothetical is identical to the one already found empty
and the candidate is skipped.

That is correct but incomplete. On an empty query string -- the first page
load, and the most common state there is -- every question is defaulted, so a
dead answer gets "Leaves no wall base." and no attribution, where the useful
sentence is 'it is the recommended "How wide?" answer'.

The fix is to give a defaulted question a real counterfactual: instead of
removing it, substitute each of its OTHER offered values, and blame it if any
of them lets the build hold.

Do not start this without a cost plan. It turns `len(others)` hypotheticals per
dead answer into `sum(len(options))` -- 3-6x -- on an endpoint already taking
1-2 seconds for around 35 offered answers, against a quarter of a second for
the parts themselves. 6-12 seconds on a 128MB Lambda is not a nicety, it is a
broken page. `_holds` is cached by predicate key, which is what makes the
current cost survivable, so any approach here should be measured against that
cache rather than assumed to benefit from it.

Context: PR #241 round 9, comment 4117009856. The `theirs` field this would
have populated was deleted in that round rather than shipped always-true.

title: [guides] a repeated query parameter cannot be refused behind the ALB
description: Found in PR #240 review. GET /api/guides/<key>/resolve refuses a question answered twice (?method=a&method=b) with a 400, because resolving one of two values would return a parts list for a question the person did not answer that way. That check cannot fire in production: an ALB collapses a repeated query key to its LAST value before Lambda sees the request, and aws_lambda_wsgi reads event['queryStringParameters'], a plain map, so the duplicate is already gone. Verified against live production by the reviewer: ?image_type=documentation&image_type=x returns 502 while ?image_type=x&image_type=documentation returns 200 — last wins. Flask would keep the FIRST value if both survived, so the dev server and production also disagree about which value they use. Making the check hold everywhere needs lambda.multi_value_headers.enabled on the target group AND an adapter that reads multiValueQueryStringParameters; enabling the target-group setting alone would 500 every request, since aws_lambda_wsgi subscripts event['queryStringParameters'] unconditionally. Options: patch/replace the adapter, or accept last-wins and delete the check. Low priority — the failure is a wrong answer for a URL nobody constructs deliberately.

title: Multi-Angle Thumbnail Viewing System
description: Enable users to view STL models from 10 isometric camera angles with interactive controls. Admins can set default viewing angles per model. System generates 10 isometric-perspective angles (6 primary directions + 4 diagonal corners) during file scan using stl-thumb --cam-pos, combined into single sprite sheet PNG. Frontend has drag-to-rotate and keyboard navigation. All angles maintain 3/4 view for depth, not flat orthographic.

title: [openforge-catalog] Every release PR conflicts because main is squash-merged
description: Observed on the 0.7.0 release: merging test into main as a squash leaves main with a commit test never saw, so the next test->main PR diffs from the pre-release merge base and GitHub reports conflicts across hundreds of files (388 on this one). The workaround each time is 'git merge -s ours origin/main' on test before opening the release PR, since main is always strictly behind in content. Options: enable merge commits on the repo so releases keep ancestry, or automate the ours-merge back into test right after each release. Compounded by GitHub not running the .beads merge driver, so .beads/issues.jsonl conflicts there even when a local merge is clean.

title: [guided builds] Stop the parser synthesising the base slot
description: Cleanup, not a fix, and not a blocker: it can land in parallel with the rest of the epic. openforge/data/metadata.py's apply_default_metadata appends a 'base' part to pieces with connection|openforge and the right shape, gated by build method (apply_openforge_wall requires build|separate wall and denies shape|floor, shape|base and build|s2w; apply_thick_wall requires build|thick wall plus component|wall). The data that produces is already correct: wall-on-tile walls have no base slot (0 of 397), nor do s2w walls (0 of 356) or s-system walls (0 of 41), and the wall-on-tile pieces that do carry one are 295 floors, 17 of them corners as well. All counts are over all 8,761 fixture records, .json and .yaml. The reason to remove it is Devon's, stated per method: within build|separate wall the slot and connection|openforge are the same fact (1,220 of 1,221; the exception carries shape|floor, which is_openforge_wall denies), and within build|thick wall likewise for the openforge walls carrying component|wall (87 of 100; the 13 without are wooden, slope and transition pieces). Across the catalog the tag alone does NOT imply a base — 4,368 records carry connection|openforge and only 2,455 of them have a base slot — so whatever replaces the slot must read the build method as well as the connection tag. Before removing: those three helpers are the only place in the repo that knows which pieces take bases under which method, so move that knowledge where the guide can read it. Verify by count afterwards: 2,499 base parts sit on 2,495 records, the three predicates account for 2,452 of those records, and the remaining 47 parts are authored and must survive — 40 in the s2w composition blueprints, 3 on dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces, and 4 in sewers.json where an authored slot sits beside a synthesised one, which is where the four duplicate base parts come from. Consumers that change meaning: src/utils/config-processing.ts, the blueprint page's compatible-bases UI, and collectDownloadUrls in src/utils/blueprint-utils.ts.
notes: Devon decided on 2026-09-19 that this lands LAST in the epic (after the guide page), not in parallel: the base rules are freshest then and it touches the blueprint page's base UI. Verification number after the parser change: 47 authored base parts on 47 records must survive (40 composition blueprints, 3 dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces, 4 sewers.json records whose authored slot sits beside a synthesised one).

title: [testing] Four test_incremental.py tests fail on PG14 locally and pass in CI
description:
Four tests in tests/test_incremental.py fail when the suite runs against a local PostgreSQL 14 cluster and pass in CI, which runs postgres:latest. They reproduce on a pristine worktree of the base branch, so they predate the guided-builds work and were not introduced by it.

Worth a look because the failure does not obviously smell like a version difference. test_process_existing_file_unchanged_preserves_images fails at 'assert len(results) == 1' with 2, and the extra record carries deprecated: True — the scanner is deprecating a file it was asked to treat as unchanged. That is the scanner mislabelling a file, which is the outcome this project cares about most, so if it is a real bug that a newer Postgres happens to mask, we want to know rather than to keep explaining the red away.

The fixture's md5 (abc123def456) does not match the md5 of the content the test writes, which is a plausible starting thread.

Found while running the suite for openforge_catalog-anc; not in that PR's scope.
notes: 2026-09-24: measured on postgres:latest in docker, which is the CI image. The four still FAIL there — so this is not a PG14-vs-latest artifact and the standing theory was wrong. Whatever differs is not the server version. Next step is to diff the actual behaviour rather than the version: they are all in TestIncrementalScanner and all concern change detection, so suspect ordering or timestamp granularity in the test setup rather than the engine.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text: Cause found 2026-09-28 (PR #247 round-3 test-coverage reviewer): the four test_incremental.py failures are timezone-dependent. They fail on this machine in MDT and pass with TZ=UTC; CI runs in UTC. Workaround for local runs: TZ=UTC pytest tests/. Fix: make the tests (or _get_file_info's local-time comparison) timezone-independent.

title: [guided builds] Feature slots: doors, torches and the rest in a guide

These are authored folder metadata, unlike the synthesised base slot removed in the parser bead, so they are real data about what a piece can take.

title: [dev] Use docker compose for Postgres instead of native clusters
description:
This project ships a docker-compose.yml at the repo root: postgres:latest on 5432, user/password/database all "openforge", data in ./db-data/. That is the intended way to get a database, and tests/conftest.py already defaults to exactly those settings (PGHOST=localhost, PGPORT=5432, PGUSER=openforge, PGPASSWORD=openforge).

I did not use it. During the guided-builds work I started five native PostgreSQL 14 clusters with pg_ctl on ports 5433-5437, one per parallel reviewer, plus an openforge_dev database for the wall guide. Devon: "development of this project was designed around using docker compose so we don't litter my OS with a bunch of crap."

What to clean up:

- five clusters still running, ports 5433 to 5437, data directories under the session scratchpad (~206M, 87M, 85M and two more), unix sockets in /tmp/pgs.*
- they are native processes, so a Docker restart does not touch them, which is how this was discovered

What to do instead:

  docker compose up -d database

Then everything uses localhost:5432 with the conftest defaults and no PG* environment variables at all. Parallel test runs, which is why I built five clusters, want a different answer under compose — separate databases inside the one container, or compose project names, rather than five servers.

Worth checking while fixing this: openforge_catalog-cib records four tests in tests/test_incremental.py that fail locally and pass in CI, and I attributed that to "local PG14 versus postgres:latest". Compose runs postgres:latest. Those four may simply pass once the database comes from compose, which would close that ticket and remove a recurring piece of noise from every full test run.
notes: 2026-09-24: two findings. (1) 'docker compose up -d database' CANNOT start as configured — the compose file hardcodes 5432:5432 and port 5432 on this machine is held by the system PostgreSQL 14 serving another project (lets_roll_* databases). Compose fails with 'address already in use'. Either the compose file needs a different host port or that system server needs to stop. (2) Worth doing regardless of tidiness: the suite runs in 29s against postgres:latest in a container versus ~170s against a native PG14 cluster, about 6x. Workaround used meanwhile, no repo changes and nothing persisted: docker run -d --name openforge-test-pg -p 5433:5432 -e POSTGRES_USER=openforge -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=openforge -e POSTGRES_DB=openforge_test postgres:latest

Zero-manual-entry defaults, curated where it matters. Payload field names/shape finalized against the HAR contract.

title: [guides] Default the parts sprite view to front-left rather than front
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30: 'shift the default view for the sprite sheet to FL'.

The guided-build parts list opens every piece at the 'front' angle (labelled F). It should open at 'front-left' (FL).

Why FL reads better for terrain: a face-on view of a wall or a floor tile is close to a flat rectangle, so the clips, the base profile and the depth of the piece are all edge-on and hard to judge. A three-quarter view shows the top face and one side at once, which is what tells you what you are actually printing.

WHERE:

    src/components/guides/guide-parts.tsx:83
        const [view, setView] = useState<string>('front');   ->  'front-left'

    src/components/guides/guide-sprite.tsx:41
        export function GuideSprite({ blueprint, view = 'front' })  ->  'front-left'

The second is the component's own fallback for callers that pass no view. Worth changing together so the default is stated once per file rather than diverging.

The name is exact: the sprite sheets carry angles named front, front-right, right, back-right, back, back-left, left, front-left, top, bottom, and src/components/sprite-controls.tsx:25 maps 'front-left' to the FL label. No new angle or regeneration is needed - every existing sheet already has it.

CHECK WHEN DOING IT: guide-sprite.tsx has a fallback for a sheet that does not carry the angle being shown (it warns and falls back to default_angle). Confirm no shipped sprite sheet lacks front-left, or that the fallback is silent enough not to fill the console. The blueprint detail viewer (src/components/blueprint/sprite-viewer.tsx) has its own default and is out of scope unless Devon wants both moved.

Also worth a look while in there: guide-parts.tsx:98 resets the view per step via stepView(), so whatever default is chosen has to survive that path too - changing only the useState initialiser may be overridden on the first step change.

title: [fixtures] Support JSONL for blueprint fixtures, and emit it as the scanner parses
description:
Two halves, in this order.

1. READ JSONL

Blueprint fixtures are currently a single JSON list (21 files) or YAML (20 files). Add .jsonl: one blueprint object per line, no enclosing list. JSON and YAML keep working — this is a third format, not a replacement.

Where it lands:
- openforge/db/fixtures/__init__.py:38 — discovery, which today accepts .json and .yaml
- openforge/db/fixtures/__init__.py:275 (_load_data) — the loader, which dispatches on suffix and raises ValueError otherwise
- openforge/app/routes/fixtures.py — _parse_fixture_data, the admin upload path, which tries JSON then falls back to YAML. bin/upload_fixture posting here is the only route a fixture has into staging and production, so JSONL has to work there too or the format cannot be deployed.
- _get_fixture_type_from_data detects a blueprint fixture by the data being a list. Parsed JSONL is also a list, so that should hold, but it wants a test rather than an assumption.

2. EMIT JSONL AS WE PARSE

openforge/data/scanner.py:751 (print_files) builds the entire result in memory, sorts it recursively, then prints one json.dumps at the end. Nothing is visible until the whole scan finishes, which on ~8,900 tiles is a long silence.

Emitting a line per blueprint as it is parsed means you can follow along, and a failure part-way leaves you with the records that did parse rather than nothing.

The thing to decide, because it is a real trade rather than an oversight: _sort_and_clean_recursively sorts the whole list by full_name for stable git diffs, and that cannot happen until every record exists. Streaming and sorted output are in tension. Options are to emit unsorted while scanning and sort in a second pass, to emit sorted-within-directory as each directory completes, or to accept unsorted JSONL and sort on read. Whichever, the git-diff stability that sorting buys should not be lost silently — it is why the sort is there.

Worth knowing: a blueprint fixture is a list of objects with file_metadata, tags, config and images, so one object per line is a natural fit. Tag descriptions and tag documentation are maps rather than lists and do not fit JSONL; they stay JSON/YAML, and the loader should say so clearly rather than producing something odd.
notes:
Deprecation reconciliation is the hard part, and it has to be handled differently before streaming is safe.

The loader decides deprecation by absence, over the complete fixture. compare_fixture_data builds fixture_keys / fixture_full_names from the whole list first, then:

- incremental.py:364 — within a namespace, any existing blueprint whose full_name is not in the fixture is deprecated
- incremental.py:455 — the legacy path, any non-deprecated model blueprint not in fixture_keys is deprecated

Both need the complete set to be meaningful. 'Not in the fixture' is only true once the fixture has ended.

The specific hazard: a JSONL file that is truncated — the scan was interrupted, the disk filled, the process was killed — is not detectably incomplete. It is a valid JSONL file that happens to be short. Loading it would deprecate every blueprint that had not yet been written, which is exactly the data loss the file format was meant to make less likely by letting you watch progress.

A JSON list has an accidental guarantee here: a truncated one fails to parse, so a partial scan cannot be loaded at all. Streaming gives that up and has to replace it deliberately. Options worth weighing: a trailer record or sidecar written only on a clean finish and required before any deprecation runs; a declared expected count checked on load; or separating the two passes so streaming output is only ever additive and deprecation is computed from a completed manifest.

Whatever is chosen, the loader should refuse to deprecate from a fixture it cannot prove is complete, rather than treating short input as authoritative.

title: [guides] Reopening a question drops keyboard focus to <body>, and aria-expanded is a literal false
description:
Found by frontend-conventions-reviewer on PR #241 (comment 4117805930), measured in jsdom + RTL at `1001857`, not reasoned. Not fixed on that PR: it is the frontend of a PR whose delta was the engine, and it was filed because three reviewers were pointed at the frontend as a whole.

## The focus half

`AnsweredStep` (`src/components/guides/guide-steps.tsx`) swaps *between* the folded button and the open `<section>` (`if (open) return ...` at ~272), so reopening a settled question unmounts the button that had focus. Measured, both directions:

```
PROBE before click    activeElement = BUTTON "How do you want to build it?Separate wall"
PROBE after expand    activeElement = BODY
PROBE after collapse  activeElement = BODY
```

Reopening a settled question is the page's central gesture. A keyboard user Tabs down, presses Enter, and lands at the top of the document — so reaching the options that just appeared means Tabbing forward through every control above them. Picking one folds the section and puts focus at the top again. Every loop re-traverses the page. A mouse user never sees it.

## The aria-expanded half

`aria-expanded={false}` is hardcoded at `guide-steps.tsx:317` and `:643`, and those are the only two `aria-expanded` in all of `src/` — this is the PR's own pattern, not one it inherited. There is no `aria-controls`, and the region the attribute would point at does not exist while the button does, because the expanded state is a different subtree. So the literal type-checks and is also a false statement: a screen reader is told "collapsed", activates the control, and the control is gone.

## The fixes the reviewer proposed

1. Drop `aria-expanded` from both buttons. This is "reopen this question", not a disclosure toggle, so the attribute only misinforms. Note before doing it: `guide-page.test.tsx` asserts `aria-expanded === 'false'` at 1733 and 1812 and selects the folded button by it at 2904, so the deletion has three test sites to update — it is a `git rm` of an attribute plus a test edit, not a one-liner.
2. Expand direction: `autoFocus={step.selected === option.key}` on the `Answer` inside the `if (open)` branch. The reviewer measured this one — `activeElement = BUTTON "Separate wall"` after the expand — and eslint is clean on it (no `jsx-a11y/no-autofocus` in this config). Landing on the answer already in force is where a keyboard user wants to be.
3. Collapse direction is **not** covered by that and needs a ref on the folded button to focus after the fold. More than a line, which is why it is in this bead and not in the PR.

Precedent for the habit: `src/components/blueprint/sprite-viewer.tsx:232` is the one place in `src/` that already calls `.focus()` deliberately.

title: exclude becomes an exact-tag allow, so a tag it hid can still be refused by a sweep
description:
Found by general-reviewer in round 6 of PR #241 (thread 4114343008), second half of that finding. The SQL half (positionless @>) was fixed in commit a93b9e9.

openforge/openapi/schemas/guide.yaml:506 promises 'Excluded tags are permitted on the piece: they are hidden, not refused', and _refinement_predicate's comment says they must not be swept either. The mechanism is the allow list, and allow is matched by exact tag while deny_children sweeps a subtree — so a tag hidden by exclude can still be refused by a sweep that exempts only its exact parent. Opposite of what the schema promises.

Spans the engine's predicate composition rather than one SQL clause, so not fixed in PR #241.

title: [guides] Opening a guide from the tab strands you outside the tabbed shell
description:
With the Guided Builds tab in place, clicking a card is a full-document navigation to `/guides/?guide=<key>`, which renders `GuidePage` on its own — no tab bar, no header, no way back except the browser button.

Found by react-hooks-reviewer in round 1 of PR #246, as an aside rather than a hooks finding. It is the same complaint `openforge_catalog-lfi` was originally about from the other direction: `guide-page.tsx` was written assuming 'there is no site nav to escape by', which is why its recovery links point at `./`. That assumption was true when `/guides` was unreachable from the catalog. It is not true now.

Two shapes of fix, neither obviously right:

1. A link back to the catalog from the guide page. Cheap, but `/guides/` is itself outside the shell, so it returns you to the entry page without the tab bar — better than nothing, still not the app.
2. Render `GuidePage` in the tab rather than `GuideEntry`, so answering happens in place. The obstacle is that the active tab is not in the URL: a card would have to link to `?guide=<key>` on `/`, and a reload would land on Part Search with a dangling parameter. Putting the tab in the query string would fix that and is a change to `tabbed-interface.tsx` that affects all four tabs.

Not urgent — the guide page works, and someone arriving from a shared link is in exactly the state it was designed for. It is the in-app path that is odd.

title: [guides] The base-clips default is hard-coded, so 1-inch builds ask for a combination that cannot exist
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30: 'there's tons of 1x1 bases, just 1x1 doesn't have all the same connector options because you can't fit more than one connector on the same face when you only have one inch' and 'I think this is because connectors aren't data driven.'

Both correct. This ticket originally said the separate-wall 1x1 cell has no wall base for any texture. That diagnosis was wrong - there are 47 wall bases at one inch, across ten textures.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. base-clips carries a hard-coded default:

    default: connection|magnetic,connection|openlock,connection|openlock|topless

MEASURED against production, wall bases carrying all three:

    width 1   0
    width 2  19
    width 3  16
    width 4  13

At one inch magnets and OpenLOCK are mutually exclusive - zero bases carry both, because they do not fit on the same face at that size. So the default names a combination that cannot exist at 1x1 and the role resolves to nothing, while 47 usable bases sit there:

    width 1, openlock + topless   11
    width 1, magnetic alone       11
    width 1, openlock alone       26
    width 1, dragonlock alone     10

THE ROOT IS THE SAME ONE AS THE TEXTURE WORK. The ANSWERS to base-clips are derived correctly - it is a from_combination refinement, so the list narrows to combinations the catalog actually has at the chosen size. It is the DEFAULT that is a fixed string, applied before anyone answers, and it is not checked against what the build can reach.

So the fix is not a 1x1 special case. The default needs to derive the same way the answers do: prefer magnets plus OpenLOCK plus topless where it exists, and otherwise fall back to the best combination available for this size. Note openforge_catalog-ume shows the same fixed-default trap on the floor guide from a different angle, and openforge_catalog-xkd is the identical shape for floor texture - a hard-coded recommendation that does not survive contact with the data.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE 'no base exists' FROM THE PAGE: the person never answered the clips question. The wizard reveals questions in order and applies the recommendation until they do, so the failure appears at 1x1 immediately, before the question that causes it is on screen.

The floor-base role is unaffected at 1x1 - only wall-base empties - which is worth checking when fixing, since square bases may carry combinations wall bases cannot.

title: [guides] Texture choices are a hand-curated list, so a new texture is invisible until someone edits a fixture
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30, after nova_trail tiles were scanned and imported and did not appear in the wall guided build: 'I never asked that to be a closed list.'

WHAT HAPPENS NOW. Both guides' texture questions carry an explicit closed 'choices' list:

    wall.yaml  texture        dungeon_stone, towne, mortar_and_stone, rough_stone,
                              cut-stone, stone_brick, aztlan, necro
    wall.yaml  floor-texture  dungeon_stone, rough_stone, cut-stone, towne, aztlan
    floor.yaml texture        dungeon_stone, rough_stone, cut-stone, towne, aztlan

A texture not on the list cannot be chosen. Answering with one is a hard 400, not a soft miss: GET /api/guides/wall/resolve?...&texture=texture|nova_trail returns 400 even though the catalog holds 188 nova_trail blueprints, 143 of them carrying build|separate wall.

So importing new tiles is not enough to surface them. Someone has to remember to edit two fixtures, and nothing fails if they forget - the tiles are simply invisible in the wizard. They remain reachable by browsing, because the question is browsable, so this is a discoverability failure rather than a correctness one.

nova_trail has been added to all three lists as a curated entry (this release), which is the stopgap, not the fix.

WHAT THE FIX LOOKS LIKE. The schema already supports it: from_namespace without 'choices' offers the whole namespace, and the engine derives the live options - _derive_choices already returns a per-answer count for from_combination refinements, narrowed to what the current build can actually reach. Making texture derive the same way would mean a scanned texture appears by itself, with a count, narrowed per method and size.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE BEFORE DOING IT, because the closed list was not arbitrary:

1. The schema says an open from_namespace is asked 'as free text' by the frontend. If that is still true, removing choices trades a wrong list for a worse control. The frontend work may be the real cost here, not the fixture change.

2. The list was curated to keep the question answerable - the schema's own note says 'a wizard asks a question you can answer by looking at it, and the namespace is not that: 40-odd textures, most of which no wall carries.' A derived list narrowed to the current build may already solve that, since most of the 40 would be empty for a given method and size and would not be offered. Worth measuring before assuming either way.

RELATED. openforge_catalog-ume is the other half of the same rot: the blurbs on those curated entries carry hand-written counts, every one now wrong. A derived list would delete both problems at once, since the count would come from the same query that produces the option.

Also openforge_catalog-9ab, which recorded that cave (46 floors) is unreachable by answering on the floor guide while aztlan (24) has a button - the same curation gap, found from the other direction.

title: [catalog] rough_stone has walls but no s2w floors or wall bases
description:
After the full regeneration on 2026-09-21, asking the wall guide for rough_stone returns a wall and nothing else:

  wall        rough_stone#wall.A.openforge.stl
  floor       NOTHING
  wall-base   NOTHING
  floor-base  NOTHING

The counts, models only, not deprecated:

  texture         walls  guide-ready  s2w floors  wall bases
  dungeon_stone    1591           82          46          35
  aztlan            237           35           8          41
  rough_stone       321           35           0           0

So rough_stone has 35 perfectly usable walls and nothing for them to stand on or beside. The floor role needs build|s2w with shape|floor|wall, and the wall base needs shape|base|wall; rough_stone has neither.

Devon: 'rough stone needs some work'. This is modelling rather than tagging — the pieces do not exist, as against existing and being tagged wrong, which was the aztlan and stone_brick story.

Note the floor half may be moot: openforge_catalog-<the mixed-texture ticket> would let a rough_stone wall stand on a dungeon_stone floor, which is how someone would build this today anyway. The wall base is the part that has no workaround.
notes:
The mixed-texture ticket referenced in the description is openforge_catalog-ltu. It would make the missing s2w floors survivable — a rough stone wall on a dungeon stone floor — but the wall base has no such workaround, which is why that half matters more.

Update 2026-09-21: the wall base now resolves. Devon: rough stone uses plain bases for now. The guide substitutes texture|plain for the rough_stone wall base, and the separate-wall option no longer demands build|separate wall of a wall base, because none of the 48 plain wall bases carries it while every other texture's does. So the remaining gap here is the s2w floors.

title: [guided builds] Audit which pieces carry a base slot and why
description: ANSWERED during PR #238 review; closed, no code change needed. The question was whether the uneven distribution of base slots was deliberate or drift. It is deliberate and fully explained by (build method, component kind, connection|openforge). Over all 8,761 fixture records: under build|separate wall, 1,220 of the 1,221 openforge walls carry the slot and the single exception carries shape|floor as well as shape|wall, which is_openforge_wall denies outright; under build|thick wall, 87 of the 100 openforge walls carry it and the 13 without are wooden, slope and transition pieces, none carrying the component|wall that is_thick_wall requires; under build|wall on tile no wall carries one and 295 floors do; under build|s2w neither floors nor scanned walls carry one, and the only s2w records with a slot are the 40 composition blueprints, where the wall part declares fulfills: base; under build|s-system nothing carries one. The three predicates account for 2,452 of the 2,495 records with a base slot; the rest are authored — 40 composition blueprints, 3 dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces whose slot no predicate produces, and 4 sewers.json records carrying an authored slot beside the synthesised one. Detail is in docs/design/guided-builds.md.
notes: Correction to the close reason above: 'the base belongs to the floor' holds for build|wall on tile only. Under build|s2w no floor carries a slot either — the only s2w records with one are the 40 composition blueprints, where the wall part declares fulfills: base — and under build|s-system nothing carries one.
close_reason: Answered by evidence during PR #238 round-2 review, no code change needed. Base-slot presence is fully explained by (build method, component kind, connection|openforge): under build|separate wall, 1,220 of the 1,221 openforge walls carry the slot and the one exception is a shape|column|low piece, not a wall; under build|thick wall, 87 of the 100 openforge walls carry it and the 13 without are component|slope pieces, which is what is_thick_wall keys on; under wall on tile, s2w and s-system no wall carries one and the base belongs to the floor (295 wall-on-tile floors, 17 of them corners too). Not drift. Detail is in docs/design/guided-builds.md.

title: Capture HAR of Thingiverse SPA create/upload/edit flow and extract API contract
description: Devon captures a HAR (Network tab, preserve log, Fetch/XHR, 'Save all as HAR with content') of a complete flow: create draft thing, set name/description/tags/category/license, upload image, upload STL, replace the STL, delete a file, publish. HAR goes to scratchpad only — contains live JWT/refresh/cookies, never commit; rotate tokens after. From the HAR, extract and document: create-thing endpoint+payload, model-file upload mechanism (direct POST vs presigned URL — matters for Lambda), file object shape incl. hash field, metadata patch, and file delete. Also verify hash algorithm: hash the exact uploaded STL locally with MD5 and SHA-256 and match against the hash Thingiverse reports (Devon guesses SHA-256). Output: docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md contract doc.
notes: LARGELY SOLVED via v1 swagger (thingiverse.com/swagger/docs/openapi.yaml) + live probes. (1) HASH = content-MD5, confirmed empirically (downloaded a file, MD5 matches the File.hash field exactly). Catalog already stores file_md5 -> sync compares directly, NO SHA-256 needed (local_sha256 column is dead/harmless). (2) WRITE AUTH SOLVED: use the 'token' field from POST /v2/auth/login as Bearer (32-char opaque, devonjones-scoped id 47139), against api.thingiverse.com DIRECTLY (www origin is Cloudflare-challenged). The env THINGIVERSE_APP_TOKEN authenticates as Joaquin (wrong account) - do not use. (3) Write surface is v1: POST /things/ (create), POST /files/0/uploadFile (multipart -> {id}), POST /files/0/FinalizeFiles, GET /things/{id}/files (hash), POST /things/{id}/publish. Full contract: docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md. REMAINING: confirm POST /things/ payload on first real create; Devon notes v1 can't set all fields he wants (open request to Thingiverse for v2 write).
close_reason: Contract captured and validated end-to-end. Write auth (login token field, devonjones-scoped, api.thingiverse.com direct), file hash = MD5 (hex or base64 depending on upload path), write endpoints (v1: POST /things/, uploadFile+FinalizeFiles, publish), filename sanitization all documented in docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md and validated against thing:7364110 (31/31 STLs match catalog file_md5).

title: Guides: request-context dataclass for _blame (10 params) and GuidePage (~148 lines)
description:
From round 7 of PR #241 (complexity-reviewer, threads 4115804996 and 4115807219), re-measured every round since. Same disposition as the round-3 extractions already in openforge_catalog-xnj. Arithmetic below is HEAD-of-round-10 (04a4d7f); the round-7 figures it replaces were stale twice over.

Python -- the recorded fix (a frozen dataclass over the trio baseline, cache, find_candidates) no longer does the job:

- _blame is now 10 positional parameters, not 8 (round 10 passed if_taken in, turning a local into a parameter). The trio takes it 10 -> 8. Still over the limit.

description: serverless-architecture-reviewer on PR #230: the ALB is ~16 USD/month of fixed cost per environment and exists only because CloudFront reaches it over HTTP. notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-28, and it matters for what this ticket implies: a function URL does NOT fix GET /api/blueprints.

The 1 MB figure in the description is the ALB response cap and is correct as far as it goes, but the failure actually observed on that route is `LAMBDA_RUNTIME Failed to post handler success response. So the payload exceeds 6 MB, not merely 1 MB, and moving to a function URL would 502 on it exactly the same way.

Nothing here argues against the migration — the cost and HTTPS reasons stand on their own, and the aws_lambda_wsgi v2-event blocker is still the real blocker. What changes is that this ticket should not be read as carrying a fix for the oversized-response route. That needs pagination, and it is -9sx.

title: [deploy] Production has no migration step; staging does — copy the job across
description:
The `Production` workflow is tests -> docker build -> `tofu apply -var image_tag=<sha>` -> S3 sync. **No step runs `bin/db_update up`.** `grep -rn db_update .github/workflows/` returns nothing; the only hits in the repo are README, package.json, `openforge/CLAUDE.md` and setup.py. So migrations are manual, which for production means the bastion.

That has been harmless until now because no merge to `main` has carried a schema change. `origin/main` is at `version_17` and has no `openforge/db/sql/guides.py` at all. The next production release therefore brings **18 (create guides) and 19 (guides.hero_image) together**, and the image is deployed before anything applies them.

Measured by migration-discipline-reviewer in round 1 of PR #246, through the real Flask client with `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` off:

    schema 19:  GET /api/guides -> 200       GET /api/guides/wall -> 200
    schema 18:  GET /api/guides -> 500 HTML  GET /api/guides/wall -> 200

The 500 is an unhandled `psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn` out of `get_all_guides`. On schema 17 it is worse — no `guides` table at all. And the entry page is now a tab in the main interface, so the failure is on the front door rather than on a route nobody has linked to.

There is no silent-corruption ordering, which is the one mercy: `load_guide_fixture` against an un-migrated database raises `UndefinedColumn` and writes nothing. The wrong order fails loudly.

Two ways to close it:

1. Write the order down and keep it manual: `bin/db_update up` then `bin/upload_fixture` (or `bin/fixtures`) on the bastion, **before** the merge that ships the image. Cheapest, and it matches how the database is operated today.
2. Add a migration step to the `Production` workflow. Needs the workflow to reach Aurora, which today it does not — the Lambda does, via `DB_SECRET_ARN`, but the runner has no path in. Bigger than it sounds.

Recorded now because PR #246 is the first change that makes it bite, and the release ritual in the production-deploy notes covers the S3 promote and says nothing about the database.
notes:
WORDING CORRECTION 2026-09-28, same as openforge_catalog-44e: where this ticket says migrations are unreachable because Aurora sits in private subnets, the mechanism is wrong even though the conclusion holds. Staging is the default VPC and all six subnets are public; what closes the door is Aurora security group, which admits only the application and bastion groups, plus the absence of a NAT for egress. A GitHub runner is outside the VPC either way, which is why the migration Lambda exists.

Also worth recording here since this is the ticket the deploy ritual is written from: PR #248 automates this for staging with a two-stage apply — tofu apply -target=aws_lambda_function.migrate, then the invoke, then the full apply that promotes the API image. The split is load-bearing: a single apply moves api.image_uri before the migration runs, which is the unhandled 500 this ticket describes. Production still uses the manual bastion ritual and should copy the split rather than a single apply.

UPDATE 2026-09-29, after the 0.8.1 release. The specific gap in the old title is CLOSED: schema 18 and 19 were applied by hand during the 0.8.0 release and main carries both, so no release is currently sitting in front of an unmigrated database. Retitled because the title read as pending work that is done.

What REMAINS, and is the actual ticket: production still has no migration step. Staging now does the whole chain on a merge to test — docker build -> tofu (migration function) -> migrate -> tofu -> frontend — built in PR #248. Production runs docker build -> tofu -> frontend and never calls bin/db_update. So the next release that DOES carry a schema change has the same 500 waiting unless someone migrates by hand first.

The work is copying staging's two resources and its job across: the migrate Lambda (same image, image_config.command at openforge/app/migrate.py, reserved_concurrency 1, PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT 120) and the split -target'ed apply that keeps the new image from going live ahead of the schema. terraform/environments/staging is kept diffable against production for exactly this.

How to tell whether a given release needs a hand migration until then, tip to tip:
    git diff --stat origin/main origin/test -- openforge/db/schema/
Empty means none. Do NOT use the three-dot form: releases are squash-merged so the merge base is stale, and it lists schema files both branches already have.

title: Fixture loader never settles on files that share an MD5
description: Loading the same blueprint fixture twice does not report zero changes. Files that are byte-identical to another file at a different path (e.g. plain#base+angled.1x1.magnetic+flex,openlock+unsupported.stl vs ...magnetic+flex.stl) are re-matched by MD5 in openforge/db/fixtures/incremental.py and classified ADDED (renamed) / ADDED (new version) on every load. Data ends up correct, but dry runs are unreadable and every load rewrites those rows. Likely cause: the full_name lookup misses paths stored in consolidated_paths, so the MD5 fallback treats a consolidated duplicate as a rename. Fix should make a repeat load of an unchanged fixture a no-op; test: load a fixture with two same-MD5 files twice and assert the second dry run is all zeros.

title: [guides] The release rule is written twice, in Python and in TypeScript
description:
Four of round 13's five findings on PR #241 are the same structural problem: a rule that exists once in `openforge/guides/resolve.py` and again in `src/services/guide-service.ts`, with no shared artifact and no test spanning the seam.

The census, from general-reviewer:
- 'does this question reach this role' — inlined four times in Python (`refinement["role"] in ("*", name)` at resolve.py:718, 1021, 1268, 1417) and as `reaches`/`narrows` in TS.
- 'which pins an answer releases' — `releasedBy` in TS, **absent in Python**. This is the P1: `/availability` sweeps a state the page's click cannot produce.
- 'which query keys are legal' — `selectionKeys` in TS, `_reject_unknown_selections` in Python. Neither reserves `guide`, which is why a step keyed `guide` makes a guide unopenable.
- 'which blueprint an md5 names' — the pin finder's lookup vs the catalog dialog's successor-chain follow. The two disagreed on the same page at the same time.
- `PIN = "part."` in both; `image_type` vs `thumbnailOf`.

Why no test catches it: `grep -rln guide integration_tests/` is empty. There is no test whose input is a React click and whose output is a Flask response. Python probes start after `answer()` has composed the request; jest probes stop before it is sent. The transformation between them is in nobody's dimension — which is also why four fuzzes over ~35,000 selection maps walked past all three click bugs: a fuzz generates inputs in the Python's vocabulary and cannot generate the transformation the TypeScript applies first.

The fix is not an integration suite. Both endpoints already receive the whole selection map, so the release rule can live in the engine and `releasedBy` becomes a call rather than a copy.

Created before merging PR #241 deliberately: the PR fixes four instances, not the class, and general-reviewer's read is that a sixth instance is likelier than not.

title: setup.py packaging: declare openforge subpackages and thingiverse template data
description: From PR #226 review (importlib-resources-reviewer, P3): setup.py's packages=['openforge'] never lists subpackages (no find_packages()) and package_data only declares openforge/db/fixtures and openforge/openapi. openforge/thingiverse/templates/*.yaml (and the thingiverse subpackage generally) ship today only because Dockerfile.api.deploy raw-copies the source tree before setup.py install. If deploy ever moves to a built wheel/sdist, package data would 404 in production only. Fix: find_packages() + package_data entry for openforge/thingiverse/templates/*.yaml. Pre-existing gap, not introduced by #226. Original comment: gh api /repos/MasterworkTools/openforge-catalog/pulls/226/comments
notes:
MERGED FROM openforge_catalog-bj5, which I filed on 2026-09-28 without checking for an existing ticket. Raised P3 -> P2 on its evidence.

Measured: a wheel built from setup.py contains openforge/__init__.py plus three bin scripts — about 4.4 KB — against 75 .py files under openforge/. packages=["openforge"] does not recurse, and package_data keys are paths rather than dotted package names, so fixtures miss too.

Nothing has failed because nothing depends on the install: CI uses pip install -e . (path-based, works), and Dockerfile.api.deploy does COPY openforge ./openforge with LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT=/var/task ahead of site-packages, so the image shadows the broken install with the real tree. The RUN python setup.py install line in that Dockerfile does nothing useful.

Why it is P2 rather than tidy-up: get_schema_versions() enumerates migrations with os.listdir, so any packaging that does not lay the modules out as files on disk yields an empty list — and before PR #248 added a head assertion that returned {"ok": true, "applied": []} and PASSED the deploy gate. A zipped or properly-packaged install would silently migrate nothing. PR #248 now raises a named error for that state, so the trap is caught rather than removed.

Fix: find_packages(include=["openforge*"]) and dotted package_data keys, then drop the setup.py install line from the Dockerfile or drop the COPY — one or the other, not both.

title: Guides: availability endpoint costs a second Lambda invocation and ~2.4s
description:
From pr-review-loop on PR #241 (serverless-architecture-reviewer, js-async-reviewer).

/availability re-composes everything /resolve does and then adds the sweep, so one user action is two Lambda invocations and ~3.1s total (resolve 0.70s + availability 2.40s). _blame multiplies the sweep by the number of answered questions with nothing bounding it. Superseded availability requests are also discarded client-side but still execute server-side.

Options considered: bound/short-circuit _blame (cheapest); merge the endpoints (rejected - would make the parts wait 3.1s instead of 0.7s); cache.

Threads: gh api /repos/MasterworkTools/openforge-catalog/pulls/241/comments/4113824255 (openforge/app/routes/guides.py:132), /4113824854 (openforge/guides/resolve.py:356), /4113820349 (src/hooks/use-guide-state.ts:91)
notes:
2026-09-28, second measurement session. Two findings, and neither points at bounding `_blame` as the first move.

**1. The cost is query planning, not the sweep's shape.** See `openforge_catalog-5ys`, which is the root cause: the same predicate takes 150ms until psycopg prepares it on the seventh call and then 12ms. Inlined literals mean production never gets there. Parameterising would take the whole endpoint to roughly a tenth without changing any semantics.

**2. `_blame` produces nothing on the shipped guide, and costs 30% of the request.** Stubbing it out: 3546ms -> 2477ms, with the same 8 dead answers still reported. And across four complete walks of `wall.yaml` with different preferences — towne, cave, largest tiles, low walls, one of them with 27 dead answers — blame named a culprit **zero times**. It returns `None` every time.

That is not a bug. The guards that make it correct are what make it silent: a removal only counts as evidence if the roles in play are unchanged and every other answer survives, and on this guide most removals truncate later steps or change what is being built. "Two answers jointly to blame and no scapegoat" is the designed outcome, and on the real catalog it is the *only* outcome.

So the interface currently renders "Leaves no Floor." and never "Leaves no Floor — it is your Width answer", while paying a third of the request for the possibility.

Three options, in the order they should be considered:

1. **Fix `-5ys` first.** Everything gets ~10x cheaper, including blame, and the question of whether blame earns its place becomes much less urgent.
2. **Then decide whether blame stays at all.** It is tested, correct, and mute. Either loosen the guards so it can name a jointly-responsible answer (a product decision about whether a probably-right culprit beats none), or delete it and keep "Leaves no Floor", which is what people actually see today.
3. **Bounding it** — the option this ticket originally recorded — is the worst of the three: it keeps the cost and the silence, and only caps the tail.

title: [guides] Let a build mix textures — a rough stone wall on a dungeon stone floor
description:
The wall guide's texture refinement applies one texture to every role at once (role: '*', with per-role substitutions for the cases where the base is a different texture by design — towne to wood, stone_brick to foundation).

That is wrong for how people actually build. Devon: "we're going to make this system capable of using different textures for the wall and floor anyway." A rough stone wall standing on a dungeon stone floor is an ordinary thing to want, and today the guide cannot express it.

It also turns a content gap into a hard stop. rough_stone has 35 usable walls and zero s2w floors (openforge_catalog-g2z), so asking for rough_stone gives a wall and no floor. If the floor could be a different texture, that build works today with the pieces that already exist.

Shape of the change, roughly:

- the refinement takes a single "role" ('*' or one name). Mixing needs the question asked more than once — a texture for the wall, a texture for the floor — which means either several refinements each naming a role, or one refinement naming a group of roles.
- "role" is a single string in openforge/openapi/schemas/guide.yaml. A list would be the smaller change, and "except_roles" already sits beside it for the floor base, which is outside the texture vocabulary entirely.
- the bases should follow their part rather than being asked separately: a wall base takes the wall's texture, a floor base is plain. The "match" mechanism already does exactly this for size, so it may extend to texture, with "substitute" continuing to handle the pairs that are deliberately different.
- the URL grows a key per textured role, and the guide page builds its query from the document's own keys, so that part follows automatically.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether the default stays one texture everywhere with the option to break it apart, or whether each role is asked independently from the start. The first is fewer questions for the common case; the second is more honest about what the catalog actually contains.

title: Download all: the iframe is torn down after 1s, aborting downloads that have not started
description:
Reported by ripsnail (NZ) on 2026-09-29: "the download all button is a bit iffy for me, I am getting NS_BINDING_ABORTED errors on some of the get requests. I would guess something to do with the timeout here getting triggered before the download starts (NZ based and downloading from a us-east server). Will likely impact people on cellular connections too."

Their diagnosis is correct and it is worse than a latency edge case.

src/utils/blueprint-utils.ts:16 downloadFiles() creates a hidden iframe per URL and removes it after a FIXED 1000 ms:

    iframe.src = url;
    document.body.appendChild(iframe);
    setTimeout(() => { document.body.removeChild(iframe); resolve(); }, 1000);

Removing an iframe whose request is still in flight aborts that request; in Firefox that is exactly NS_BINDING_ABORTED.

MEASURED against production 2026-09-29, GET /api/blueprints/<id>/download (which 302s to a presigned R2 URL):

    cold Lambda : 5.03 s to issue the 302
    warm        : 0.35 s, 0.35 s

The iframe lives 1.0 s. So on a cold start the redirect has not even been issued when the iframe is destroyed — the download fails for EVERYONE, not only distant users. Production cold start was separately measured at Init Duration 2419 ms, so this is not rare.

Warm is 0.35 s measured from a low-latency client, and that is only the redirect: the browser must then open a new TLS connection to R2 and begin the transfer before the iframe dies. Add NZ round trips (~200 ms each way to us-east) or cellular and the 1 s budget is gone. Hence "some of the get requests" — the later files in the batch are also racing the next iframe, since creation is staggered by index*1000 ms while each lives 1000 ms, so iframe N is removed exactly as iframe N+1 is created.

This is the cause of openforge_catalog-ptt, which predicted on 2026-09-27 that the button "cannot tell you it got N-1". A real user has now hit precisely that silent partial failure, which argues for doing both together.

FIX OPTIONS, cheapest first:
- Remove the iframe on its load/error event with a long fallback (30-60 s) instead of a fixed 1 s. One-line-ish, removes the race.
- Better: resolve the 302 first (fetch with redirect: "manual"), then point an <a download> or the iframe straight at the presigned R2 URL, taking the Lambda out of the download critical path entirely.
- Either way, report per-file success so -ptt is closed at the same time.

Worth testing the fix by throttling the network rather than on a fast connection, because a fast warm client is exactly the configuration where the current code appears to work.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-29, from the review of PR #251. Three claims in the description above are wrong, and two numbers in this note were wrong in its first version.

1. The stagger race does not exist. The description says creation was staggered by index*1000 ms while each iframe lived 1000 ms, so iframe N was removed as iframe N+1 was created, and the later files raced hardest. False. The old loop was 'await downloadWithDelay(urls[i], i)' — fully sequential — so the index*1000 delay ran AFTER the previous iframe had already been removed. Replayed under a virtual clock the timeline is: create /a t=0, remove t=1000, create /b t=2000, remove t=3000, create /c t=5000, remove t=6000. No two iframes ever coexisted and the gap grew. Every file had an identical 1000 ms budget. Independently re-derived from 'git show origin/test:src/utils/blueprint-utils.ts' by a second reviewer, including the 1000*(1+2+...+N) total: 21000 ms predicted for six files against 21082/21457 ms measured.

2. 'A cold start failed for everyone' is overstated, but the first version of this correction then overstated in the other direction. It said 'files 2..N ran against the container that first iframe had warmed'. That is not reliable either: a client-side abort does not cancel the ALB->Lambda invocation it started, and file 2 is created at t=2000 ms while a ~4 s cold invocation is still running, so file 2 can get its own cold environment and die at t=3000 ms just as file 1 did. Fan-out to fresh environments is exactly what the 712/731/747/3753/4750/5123 ms trace below shows. All that is safely claimable: a cold start did not fail every file, and single-file downloads take the nav() path, never an iframe, so they were never exposed at all. How many of files 2..N died depended on Lambda's placement, not on a rule.

3. The timings in the description are slightly off. Re-measured on production 2026-09-29 by two reviewers independently: 4.72 s and 4.12 s cold, 0.27-0.39 s warm — not 5.03 s and 0.35 s. Same order, and either way a 1000 ms iframe could not survive a cold start.

What ripsnail actually hit: a 1000 ms budget too short for a file whose request landed on a cold environment, and too short for any file once NZ round trips or cellular latency are added. 'Some of the get requests' fits that, not an overlap race.

The fix is unaffected — 1000 ms was too short on every file's own terms — but the mechanism as written sends a future reader hunting a stagger bug that never existed.

MEASURED end-to-end AFTER THE SHIPPED FIX, real browsers against production, 6 blueprints, 3 runs per engine, counting browser download-start events: 6/6 every run, last handoff 27 ms in Chromium and 55 ms in Firefox. main is 5/6 in both engines at ~21 s.

  CORRECTION to the first version of this paragraph: it credited the shipped fix with '2008 ms (Chromium) and 2255 ms (Firefox)'. Those are the numbers for a WITHDRAWN intermediate version of the fix that probed each URL with fetch(redirect: 'manual') before creating its iframe. That probe was deleted during review, so those figures describe code that does not exist. The shipped function performs no I/O at all, which is why its handoff is ~75x faster.

One run's arrival times were 712, 731, 747, 3753, 4750, 5123 ms: the last three landed on cold execution environments with no warming ahead of them and all six files still arrived, because the 60 s lifetime absorbs a cold start. That is the mechanism of the fix, stated as a measurement rather than a theory.

Caveat on what 'delivered' means there: the harness counts download-start events and cancels the transfer, so it measures 6 requests that became downloads, not 6 completed files. That is the right oracle for this bug, which is about requests that never start, but it does not test a transfer still in flight when the iframe is removed at 60 s. That case rests on a response that has become a download no longer being owned by the iframe, which is now stated in the code comment.

Also: this does NOT close openforge_catalog-ptt. _get_signed_urls (openforge/app/routes/blueprints.py:171) calls generate_presigned_url, which signs locally with no head_object and no network call, so a stale storage_address presigns cleanly and then 403s at R2 with nothing detecting it. See ptt for what can and cannot be reported.

CORRECTION to the FIX OPTIONS in the description above, 2026-09-29 (round 5 of PR #251). The second option as written cannot be built: "resolve the 302 first (fetch with redirect: 'manual'), then point an <a download> or the iframe straight at the presigned R2 URL". A redirect: 'manual' fetch yields an opaque-redirect FILTERED response — status 0 and an EMPTY header list — so the client can never read Location out of it, and there is no presigned URL to point anything at. That shape is only usable as a yes/no signal, which is how the withdrawn probe used it.

Getting the URL client-side would need a backend endpoint that returns it as JSON instead of redirecting. Worth knowing before anyone tries: this is the same species of error as openforge_catalog-ptt's option (b), which claimed a client could HEAD a GET-presigned URL when SigV4 folds the method into the signature.

WHAT SHIPPED, for the record: option 1 (a long lifetime instead of a fixed 1000 ms), plus per-file reporting via the iframe's own load event rather than via a pre-flight request. Option 2 was attempted and withdrawn; option 3's on-screen half remains openforge_catalog-ptt.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #251, squash-merged to test as 8487f14 on 2026-09-29.

SHIPPED: the download iframe lives 60 s instead of a fixed 1000 ms, plus a load listener on each iframe that reports a download failing past the redirect. Measured in Chromium and Firefox against production, 3 runs each on 6 blueprints: 6/6 became downloads every run, versus 5/6 on main. One run's arrivals were 712/731/747/3753/4750/5123 ms, so three requests landed on cold execution environments with no warming ahead of them and all six still arrived.

NOT shipped, and withdrawn during review: a pre-flight fetch(redirect: 'manual') per file. See the correction notes above for why, and for the two claims in this ticket's original description that were false.

STILL OPEN and deliberately not closed by this: openforge_catalog-ptt, the on-screen half. The load listener is the detection half only, and it sees only failures that commit a document — an unreachable R2 host, an empty-bodied 403 and a mid-transfer reset are all silent in Firefox.

Five review rounds, 41 threads, no round found a P1 or P2 in the download logic itself.

title: [loader] The fixture upload loads the whole catalog's images into a 128 MB Lambda
description:
_load_existing_blueprints hands get_images_for_blueprints every id from get_non_deprecated_blueprints — the entire catalog — regardless of how small the uploaded fixture is, and nothing chunks it. That runs in the Lambda, because POST /api/admin/fixtures/blueprints is how bin/upload_fixture puts blueprints into staging and production.

Measured by a reviewer through psycopg against tables built from the real fixtures (8,721 blueprints, 84,221 tag rows, 8,720 images, every one carrying sprite_metadata), tracemalloc around the fetchall()s:

  before openforge_catalog-anc: 59.0 MB resident (images alone 6.8 MB)
  after:                        94.2 MB resident (images alone 41.9 MB)

Importing the Flask app costs ~60 MB RSS before a row is fetched, and memory_size is 128. 60 + 94 does not fit; 60 + 59 barely did.

Not a regression in outcome — before the sprite_metadata fix that path was broken a different way, reporting every blueprint changed and then deleting and reinserting 8,720 images inside a 30 second timeout, which dies on the clock before it dies on the heap. But it is now broken on memory too, and the fix is a deletion one level up: the loader needs tags and images only for the blueprints the fixture names. The full-catalog sweep exists to find deprecations, which needs id and full_name and nothing else. That takes 94 MB to single digits and keeps it there.

See also openforge_catalog-gvw (tuning Lambda memory), which would paper over this rather than fix it.

Found by the serverless-architecture-reviewer on PR #240.

title: [loader] Three blueprints in the fixtures are absent from production
description:
RETRACTED AND REWRITTEN 2026-09-30. This ticket was filed as a P1 claiming bin/fixtures reports additions it never applies, and that both environments were missing 367 blueprints. BOTH CLAIMS WERE WRONG.

What was actually wrong with the evidence: I compared the loader's pending list against blueprints.full_name and called every non-match absent. A file byte-identical to another at a different path is not a separate row - the loader keeps one blueprint per MD5 and records the other paths in consolidated_paths. So the content was in the catalog; my query was looking in the wrong column. The lead came from the catalog-scanner session, which had measured the same behaviour independently and filed openforge_catalog-jlw.

MEASURED against production, of the 533 entries the loader reports as pending:

    166  matched directly by full_name
    364  present inside another row's consolidated_paths
      3  genuinely absent
    ---
    533

Additions also plainly do apply: the nova_trail release loaded 147 rows from nova_trail.json and 373 from bases.json, both landing in production.

THE 364 ARE NOT THIS TICKET. They are openforge_catalog-jlw: the loader re-matches consolidated duplicates as 'ADDED (renamed)' / 'ADDED (new version)' on every run, so the pending count never converges even on a database that is completely current. That is a reporting defect, not missing data, and jlw has the sharper reproduction - localhost still dry-runs Added: 180 against a bases.json it has already loaded.

WHAT REMAINS, and is all this ticket is now about - three blueprints listed in the fixtures with no row and no consolidated path in production:

    tiles/cave/floors/floor%aggregate/openforge/cave%aggregate+squares#floor.1x1.openforge.stl
    tiles/cave/floors/floor%aggregate/openlock/cave%aggregate+squares#floor.1x1.openlock.stl
    tiles/mines/thick_wall/wooden_walls/mine#wall,wooden.IO.openforge.stl

Two cave aggregate 1x1 floors and one wooden mine wall. Worth finding out whether they fail to load for a shared reason or are three unrelated skips; three is small enough that the answer is probably visible in one run with verbose output.

Dropped P1 -> P3. Nothing is broken for a user: both guides resolve without empty roles in production, and the catalog is not missing the content I said it was.

WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE, since this is the second time on this project that a confident claim about missing data was really a wrong query: check the schema for where else the value could live before concluding something is absent. consolidated_paths exists precisely because this catalog's files move and duplicate, which is the first thing CLAUDE.md says about it.

title: No fixture can be uploaded to a deployed environment: YAML is base64-mangled and JSON over ~3.5 MB is rejected
description:
Measured against staging on 2026-09-28, dry_run=true so nothing was written. Both halves block the PR #247 release, which needs 14 blueprint JSON fixtures, 4 s2w YAML compositions and guides/wall.yaml loaded into staging.

HALF ONE — EVERY YAML FIXTURE FAILS, and bin/upload_fixture is what sends the bad header.

    Content-Type: application/x-yaml  -> 500 {"error":"Cannot determine fixture type for data of type str"}
    Content-Type: application/json    -> 500 {"error":"uploaded guide: ... steps is a required property"}
    Content-Type: text/plain          -> same as application/json

The second and third are the CORRECT behaviour: the body parsed to a dict, was identified as a guide, and reached schema validation (my probe payload was deliberately incomplete). Only x-yaml fails, and it fails by producing a str.

_parse_fixture_data branches on the content type but both branches end at the same safe_load(raw_data), so identical bytes cannot yield a str in one branch and a dict in the other. Therefore raw_data itself differs by content type — i.e. the ALB-to-WSGI adapter (aws_lambda_wsgi) leaves the body base64-encoded for content types it does not classify as text, and safe_load of a base64 blob is a plain scalar, which is exactly "type str". Confirmed by elimination rather than by reading the adapter; the same request fails identically straight at the ALB, so CloudFront is not involved.

bin/upload_fixture sets application/x-yaml for any .yaml/.yml (case at line ~140), so every YAML fixture upload to a deployed environment has always been broken. It has never been noticed because YAML fixtures are new-ish and the guide fixture was loaded another way.

Workaround that works today: send YAML with Content-Type application/json and let the route JSONDecodeError-fallback into safe_load. Real fix: decode per isBase64Encoded in the adapter path, or normalise in _parse_fixture_data, plus an integration test that posts a YAML fixture through the real event shape rather than the Flask test client.

HALF TWO — JSON FIXTURES OVER ROUGHLY 3.5 MB ARE REJECTED AT THE EDGE.

    towne.json          3.5M -> HTTP 413 Request Entity Too Large
    dungeon_stone.json   14M -> HTTP 413

Not the app: an HTML 413 from in front of it. The 14 blueprint fixtures total 42 MB, with dungeon_stone.json at 14 MB alone, so most of the release cannot go through the endpoint at any content type. Related to openforge_catalog-9sx, which is the same class of limit in the response direction.

THE PATH THAT WORKS, and how the wall guide was actually loaded: bin/fixtures against the database directly, from the bastion or through an SSH tunnel, using DB_SECRET_ARN or the bastion bin/.env. That bypasses the app entirely and has no size limit. It requires a checkout whose schema matches the deployed code.

Filed P1 because a release is waiting on it and the failure mode of the YAML half is silent-looking: a 500 mentioning "type str" reads like a bad fixture rather than a transport bug.

description: package.json's 'dev' script runs 'concurrently pnpm run next-dev / pnpm run flask-dev' while the repo has only package-lock.json and every workflow now uses npm (#232).
