title: [openforge-catalog] The version in the page header is a hand-kept copy of package.json
description: src/components/main-content-wrapper.tsx hardcodes 'Version 0.7.0' next to package.json's version field, so a release has to remember both and they can drift silently. Read it from package.json at build time through next.config.js's env block, the same way NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_GENERATOR_URL is handled.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #246. `next.config.js` reads the version out of `package.json` and exposes it as `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` through the `env` block — the same mechanism `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_GENERATOR_URL` already used, which is what this ticket suggested. `main-content-wrapper.tsx` renders that instead of a literal, so there is no second copy to keep.

Baked in at build time rather than read at runtime, because this is a static export: there is no server to ask, and the number on the page now cannot drift from the bundle it was built with, since it is part of that bundle. Verified by building: `0.8.0` appears in `out/index.html` and in the page chunk, and no version literal remains anywhere in `src/`.

Prompted by Devon noticing the bump to 0.8.0 took two hand edits and asking whether a static site should be doing it that way at all. It should not.

title: Download all N files cannot tell you it got N-1
description: Found by silent-failure-hunter in round 6 of PR #241 (thread 4114292186), P3, pre-existing. guide-parts.tsx:163 onClick={() => downloadFiles(urls)} — the button says how many files it will fetch and has no way to report a partial result. Same shape as the established blueprint-container.tsx:48 call site, so it is the house pattern rather than this PR's doing, and src/CLAUDE.md sets frontend error handling at console-log for the beta.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND, and the predicted failure has now happened to a real user. openforge_catalog-m8i is the mechanism: downloadFiles() removes each hidden iframe after a fixed 1000 ms, which aborts any request that has not yet started transferring — NS_BINDING_ABORTED in Firefox. Measured on production: the /download redirect takes 4.1-4.7 s on a cold Lambda and 0.27-0.39 s warm, against a 1 s budget. (Originally recorded as 5.03 s / 0.35 s; re-measured twice during the review of PR #251.)

ripsnail reported it from New Zealand on 2026-09-29: 'getting NS_BINDING_ABORTED errors on some of the get requests'. 'Some' is the tell — a partial result, which is exactly what this ticket said the button could not report.

Raised P3 -> P2 and worth doing with openforge_catalog-m8i rather than after it: fixing the race without reporting leaves the next partial failure just as silent, and reporting without fixing the race just surfaces a failure that should not be happening.

[The three paragraphs above were accidentally overwritten on 2026-09-29 by a bd update --notes whose append trick silently produced an empty string, and are restored here from the pre-overwrite read. --notes REPLACES; it does not append.]

UPDATE 2026-09-29, from the review of PR #251. That PR fixes the race but does NOT unblock this, contrary to what its description originally claimed.

An earlier version of #251 probed each URL with fetch(url, {redirect: 'manual'}) and returned {started, failed}, which looked like it supplied the information this ticket needs. It does not, and it was deleted:

_get_signed_urls (openforge/app/routes/blueprints.py:171) calls generate_presigned_url, which signs LOCALLY with no head_object and no network call. The only head_object in the tree is openforge/data/io.py:158, scanner-side. So a pre-flight against /api/blueprints/<id>/download can only ever see a 400 (malformed uuid) or a 404 — and the 404 has four causes, not one: CLOUDFLARE_ENDPOINT unconfigured, storage_address is None, file_name is None, or the blueprint is absent. collectDownloadUrls screens only the file_name case client-side; storage_address is nullable (README.md:162) and is NOT screened.

The failure that actually happens in this project is a stale storage_address — files move and get renamed as a matter of normal workflow. That presigns cleanly, returns a valid 302, and then 403s at R2 inside a hidden iframe. Nothing client-side observed it.

OPTIONS, corrected 2026-09-29 after review found two of the three originally listed here were wrong:

(a) The backend verifies the object exists (head_object) before presigning. Real, and the most complete. Cost to state plainly: one R2 round trip PER FILE inside the Lambda, on the cold-start path, on a 128 MB function — the CLAUDE.md cost constraint pushes back on this.

(b) The client HEADs the presigned R2 URL. PROBABLY NOT VIABLE, and it was wrong to list it as a peer of (a). SigV4 folds the HTTP method into the canonical request, so a HEAD against a GET-presigned URL is a signature mismatch; it would need a separately presigned HEAD, which collapses (b) into (a). It would also need R2 bucket CORS, which is a Cloudflare-dashboard change outside this tree — the only CORS in the repo is flask_cors gated to localhost (openforge/app/index.py:26). Marked verify-before-relying-on rather than asserted.

(c) Accept that only reachability-to-the-API is knowable and say so precisely, rather than implying delivery.

(d) NEW, and the cheapest: listen to the iframe's own load event. This observes the actual download rather than a separate request, so it adds no invocation and cannot fail closed. MEASURED in Chromium and Firefox, 3 trials each: a 302 that ends in an R2 403 fires load with contentDocument === null in both engines, while a successful download fires either no event (Chromium) or load with a readable empty document (Firefox). So the discriminator is load plus CONTENT, which has two forms: an unreadable document (null, the cross-origin R2 refusal) or a readable non-empty one (our own API's error body, printed). load alone is wrong, and so is "load plus an unreadable document" — an earlier version of this note said that, which would have missed every same-origin failure including the ALB 5xx mentioned below, since a rendered 5xx body is readable. Attaching the listener did not disturb the transfer. Ceiling: high precision, PARTIAL recall — it sees a rendered error page, not a cancelled or reset transfer. Landed in #251 as a console warning; the on-screen half is still this ticket.

Why (d) mattered enough to land immediately: for the R2-refusal class Chromium logs 'Failed to load resource: 403' but FIREFOX LOGS NOTHING AT ALL — no console message, no requestfailed. ripsnail is the Firefox reporter, so before #251 that failure class was not merely unreported, it was undetectable in the browser of the person who raised it.

STILL OPEN HERE: putting any of this on screen. src/CLAUDE.md sets frontend error handling at console-log for the beta, so #251 logs and does not render.

ALSO FOLDED IN (js-async-reviewer, #251 thread 4135113925): the button has no pending state and stays clickable while downloads are handed off, so a double-click fans a second full batch — duplicate files and double the invocations. Same root as this ticket: the button reports nothing about what it is doing.
  Corrected 2026-09-29: an earlier version of this paragraph said 'both call sites float the promise' and 'returns in 11-55 ms rather than seconds', which described the withdrawn probe version. downloadFiles is synchronous and returns void now, so there is no promise to float and it returns in ~0 ms always — which means the double-click window is the ENTIRE in-flight period of the batch, unbounded, rather than the narrow window that wording implied. Worse than it read, not better.

ALSO (serverless-architecture-reviewer, #251): a Lambda throttle is a third invisible failure. reserved_concurrent_executions = 50 is shared with all API traffic, so roughly 8 simultaneous Download-alls at N=6 exhausts it; a throttled request surfaces as an ALB 5xx inside a hidden iframe, which nothing observes. Option (d) catches this one too, since a 5xx body renders in the frame.

title: [images] The scanner deletes a documentation image it did not put there
description:
POST /api/images accepts image_type: documentation together with blueprint_ids, so a curated documentation image can be linked to a blueprint in blueprint_images. The incremental loader then puts it on the existing side, no fixture will ever carry it, the two sides differ, and _handle_modification calls delete_images_for_blueprint (every link, not just thumbnails) and reinserts only the fixture's images. So the curated link is deleted, and the blueprint reports changed again on the next scan — the same always-changed loop that openforge_catalog-anc just fixed for ordinary blueprints, but for a case the fix does not reach.

Reproduced by a reviewer against the real comparison: existing = [thumbnail, documentation], fixture = [thumbnail] -> changed? True.

Not reachable from the UI today — nothing in src/ sends blueprint_ids — which is why it is not a P1.

The fix is cheap now that image_type is in the batch projection: filter the existing side to the images the scanner can own (image_type == 'thumbnail') before building existing_images, and give delete_images_for_blueprint the same restriction. image_type then stops being a field the comparison excludes and becomes the field that says which images the scanner owns.

Found by the general-reviewer on PR #240.

title: Delete the hand-built staging API resources after tofu adopts staging
description:
Cleanup after the first successful apply of openforge_catalog-9xz. None of these can be imported into the production-shaped resources, so tofu creates correct ones alongside and these are left orphaned:

- Lambda function Openforge-Catalog-API (tofu creates openforge-catalog-api; function_name is ForceNew and the deploy role cannot manage IAM outside openforge-catalog-*)
- its role Openforge-Catalog-API-role-ogdz6ix0, under the service-role path
- log group /aws/lambda/Openforge-Catalog-API, which has no retention set (tofu sets 30 days on the new one)
- target group lambda-ny4k7jkm5v7dd0as80u, a console leftover nothing forwards to
- the port 443 HTTPS listener on the openforge-catalog ALB, unused: CloudFront reaches the ALB with OriginProtocolPolicy http-only on port 80, and production models only the port 80 listener

Do not delete any of it until staging.openforge.tools serves /api/guides from the new function. The old function is the rollback.
notes:
UNBLOCKED 2026-09-28 23:56 — the precondition this ticket waited on is met, and the commands are below. I could not run them: the deletions were refused by my own guardrail as irreversible, so they need a human.

PRECONDITION SATISFIED, verified live after the adoption apply:
  ALB target group openforge-catalog-api now points at openforge-catalog-api (the new function)
  staging.openforge.tools/api/guides -> 200 with the wall guide and its hero_image
  /api/guides/wall -> 200, /api/guides/wall/resolve -> 200 (14,670 b)
  POST /api/blueprints/tags -> 200 (38,757 b)
  new function Max Memory Used 106-107 MB of 128, matching production
  stray target group has 0 registered targets
  CloudFront reaches the ALB OriginProtocolPolicy http-only, so the 443 listener is unused
  0 Route53 hosted zones in this account, so nothing resolves to the ALB by name

THE COMMANDS, in this order (each is AWS_PROFILE=staging):

  # 1. the console-leftover target group, nothing forwards to it
  aws elbv2 delete-target-group --target-group-arn \
    arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:682033461796:targetgroup/lambda-ny4k7jkm5v7dd0as80u/b251d42f4101f1a2

  # 2. the unused 443 listener (tofu models only port 80, so this is permanent drift otherwise).
  #    Deleting it does not touch its ACM certificate.
  aws elbv2 delete-listener --listener-arn \
    arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:682033461796:listener/app/openforge-catalog/67abed33a99d7bf7/2fd818a82e14695a

title: [types] Blueprint.storage_address is declared non-null but the column is nullable, and guide-service types the same field correctly
description:
Found by silent-failure-hunter during review of PR #251.

src/types.ts:56 declares storage_address: string on Blueprint. The database column is nullable (README.md:162), and src/services/guide-service.ts:159 types the same field on its own interface as string | null. So the two disagree and the stricter one is the wrong one.

Consequence: tsc cannot warn about the case that actually occurs. A blueprint row with file_name set and storage_address NULL is a real, reachable state, and openforge/app/routes/blueprints.py:171 _get_signed_urls bare-returns on it, after which download_blueprint abort(404)s. Client-side, collectDownloadUrls (src/utils/blueprint-utils.ts) screens only file_name and never storage_address — and cannot be asked to, because the type says the field is always present. Every call site that reads it is implicitly asserting something the schema does not guarantee.

This is the sibling of the stale-storage_address case discussed on openforge_catalog-ptt: same field, same 404, but this one is a missing value rather than a value pointing at a moved object. PR #251 added an iframe load listener that now reports both when they happen, so this is about preventing them rather than seeing them.

FIX: change src/types.ts:56 to string | null, then follow tsc to the call sites and decide each one. Expect collectDownloadUrls to gain a storage_address check alongside its existing file_name one, which would stop offering a download that is guaranteed to 404.

Worth doing carefully rather than quickly: widening the type will surface every place that assumed non-null, and some of those may deserve a real fix rather than a null check.

title: [dropbox] Rename tiles/aztlan/separate_walls to separate_wall

title: Staging docker-build's push step is gated on an input that cannot exist
description:
`.github/workflows/staging.yaml` gates the image push on `if: ${{ ! inputs.use_cache }}`. That workflow triggers only on `push: branches: [test]`, and `inputs` exists only for `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` — so the expression evaluates against an undefined context every run.

It happens to work today (the negation of an undefined value is truthy, so the push runs), which is why nobody has noticed. The hazard is that `docker-build` reports success either way: if the expression ever evaluated false, the job would go green having pushed nothing, and four downstream jobs now assume the tag is in ECR. Before PR #248 the only consumer was a frontend sync that did not care; now `tofu-apply-migrate`, `migrate`, `tofu-apply` and `frontend-deploy` all depend on that image existing.

Fix: delete the condition, or add a `workflow_dispatch` input named `use_cache` with a default so the expression means something.

Found by the general-reviewer on PR #248 (P3, pre-existing, flagged because the round-2 changes made it load-bearing).

title: [guides] The wall guide offers two building-facade textures whose walls it structurally excludes
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30: 'it's the building facades, and those don't ship any non sidelock walls.'

mortar_and_stone and stone_brick are on the wall guide's texture list and can never produce a wall there.

MEASURED, separate-wall walls by connector:

    stone_brick        76 walls, 76 carry connection|side
    mortar_and_stone   40 walls, 20 carry connection|side
    nova_trail        143 walls, 47 side
    dungeon_stone    1370 walls, 607 side

The wall role's query is deny_children: [connection] with allow: [connection|openforge, connection|openlock]. connection|side is not spared, so every sidelock wall is swept. For stone_brick that is all of them.

CONSEQUENCE: picking either texture renders 'Nothing in the catalog matches this combination yet' across most methods and sizes. Measured over 216 cells (3 methods x 8 sizes x 9 textures), these two are the only textures producing dead cells other than the all-texture separate-wall 1x1 case (openforge_catalog-f8l).

This is not new and was not introduced by adding nova_trail, which empties nothing the other textures do not.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and they are different products:

1. Take them off the list. Honest and immediate: the guide stops offering builds it cannot make. Loses building facades from guided builds entirely.

2. Teach the wall role about sidelock. Building facades are a real part of the catalog and a wall guide that cannot offer them is incomplete. That means allowing connection|side, and probably a step or refinement asking how the wall connects, since mixing sidelock and openlock walls in one build is not something the guide currently reasons about.

Worth deciding deliberately rather than by deletion - openforge_catalog-g1g would make the list derive from the catalog, and a derived list would drop these two automatically for the wrong reason, hiding the question rather than answering it.

MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-09-30, after the full fixture import, which narrows the claim above. Sweeping all 3 methods x 8 sizes:

    mortar_and_stone   18 of 24 cells dead
    stone_brick        18 of 24 cells dead
    rough_stone         1 of 24 (the universal separate-wall 1x1 case)
    nova_trail          1 of 24 (same)

So 'can never produce a wall there' is too strong. The dead cells are wall-on-tile and s2w; both textures DO resolve on separate-wall, which is presumably where their non-sidelock pieces live. The earlier measurement was taken against localhost before the full import and read as total failure.

Still worth fixing - three quarters of the offered combinations are dead for these two - but a patron who picks separate-wall gets a working build.

title: setup.py declares no package data that actually matches; prod works only via Dockerfile COPY
description:
Found by importlib-resources-reviewer in round 6 of PR #241 (thread 4114284379).

setup.py has packages=['openforge'] (no subpackages) and package_data={'openforge/db/fixtures': ['*.json','*.yaml'], 'openforge/openapi': ['*.yaml']}. The keys are path-style rather than dotted package names, so they match nothing; and openforge/db/fixtures/guides/wall.yaml is in a separate package (openforge.db.fixtures.guides) that '*.yaml' would not reach even with the right key.

Proven by building a wheel from the branch: 8 entries total, openforge/__init__.py only, zero .yaml/.json, zero subpackages. 'python setup.py install' likewise installs only site-packages/openforge/__init__.py.

It works in production only because Dockerfile.api.deploy does 'COPY openforge ./openforge' into WORKDIR /var/task with no .dockerignore, and CI uses 'pip install -e .'. So the one thing between production and 'schema file not found' is a COPY line: a cold-start cleanup that switched to 'pip install .' would silently drop every guide fixture and every OpenAPI schema.

Suggested fix: find_namespace_packages(include=['openforge','openforge.*']) plus package_data={'openforge': ['**/*.yaml','**/*.json','**/*.sql']}. Namespace variant because openforge/openapi/schemas/ has no __init__.py.

Pre-existing, so not fixed in PR #241.

title: [api] A NUL byte in a path argument answers 500 rather than 400
description:
Now that lambda_handler decodes the path, %00 in a path segment becomes a real NUL, reaches psycopg as a query parameter and raises DataError, which Flask answers as a 500. A NUL in a URL is never legitimate input, so a 400 is the honest answer and a 500 is noise in the error metric.

Scope is the whole API, not the guide endpoints. _decode_alb_event decodes the path for every route, so /api/tag-documentation/a%00b 500s too, where on the test branch all of these are 404s. Verified by a reviewer with TESTING=False, so it is a 500 rather than an escaped exception — the earlier note that it escaped the handler was an artefact of the test fixture leaving TESTING=True.

Left out of openforge_catalog-anc because refusing it means giving _decode_alb_event an error-return path, which turns one job into two (decode, and refuse). Worth doing as its own small change at that boundary alongside whatever else wants validating there.

Found by the error-handling-reviewer on PR #240.

title: The staging deploy gate has no test and is about to be copied to production
description:
The `migrate` job in `.github/workflows/staging.yaml` decides whether a deploy proceeds, in inline Python inside a heredoc. It has two failure branches and no pytest coverage, and `pytest tests/` cannot reach it.

It is correct today. Two reviewers extracted the real heredoc (through a YAML parser, so the indentation stripping is the genuine thing) and ran it against payloads between them: healthy with versions applied, healthy no-op, `before: null`, `FunctionError`, empty `response.json`, non-JSON, missing `ok`, missing `applied`, `"ok": "true"` as a string, payload `null`, payload a list, empty `invoke.json`, `ok: false`. Exit 0 on the three good shapes, exit 1 on every malformed one. It fails closed.

The reason to ticket it anyway: the named surviving mutant is `is not True` -> `is False`, which lets `{}` and `null` through and promotes a frontend in front of an unmigrated database — and `CLAUDE.md` says this job is to be copied to production, so the untested copy becomes two. The payload contract also just changed once already (`applied` went from a bool to a list of versions), which is exactly the kind of change a test would have caught if the gate had drifted.

Shape of the fix: move the logic to `bin/check_migrate_invoke.py` reading the two files, so the workflow step is one call and the branches are unit-testable, or a `_gate(meta, payload)` helper with a small test module.

Filed because I replied "accepted, not fixed" on the round-1 thread without a ticket, and the test-coverage reviewer correctly pointed out that the contract does not allow that.

title: [guides] Changing an answer folds the question back showing the answer you just replaced
description:
Found by frontend-conventions-reviewer on PR #241 (comment 4117807815), measured in jsdom + RTL at `1001857` with `/resolve` held open. Not fixed on that PR.

`AnsweredStep`'s `onPick` calls `onOpenChange?.(null)` (`src/components/guides/guide-steps.tsx:290`), which is local state and lands this tick. `step.selected` comes from `/resolve` and lands a round trip later. So the fold is immediate and its label is the old value:

```
PROBE in-flight buttons = ["How do you want to build it?Separate wall"]
PROBE after landing     = ["How do you want to build it?Modular (s2w)"]
```

You reopened the question, clicked **Modular**, and the section closed and said **Separate wall** — not "loading", not the old answer greyed, but the old answer stated plainly as the settled result. Warm Lambda: a flicker. Cold start (a standing cost per root CLAUDE.md): seconds of the page asserting the opposite of what you just did, and the obvious response is to reopen and click again.

`OpenStep` has the milder version: `chosen={false}` is hardcoded, so a first answer to any question produces no visible change until the resolution lands. Nothing wrong is on screen there, only nothing happens — which is why the folded case is the one filed.

Two shapes, neither measured by the reviewer:

- Don't fold until the resolution agrees: leave `opened` set and let the fold happen when the new `step.selected` arrives. Smallest diff; the reopened section stays open a beat longer, which reads as "still deciding" rather than as a wrong answer.
- Or surface the in-flight resolve from `useGuideState` — it already knows — and let the folded label render the pending selection instead of the stale one.

Ruled out as making it worse, checked rather than assumed: clicking the same answer twice is a no-op (identical `replaceState` search string, `useSyncExternalStore` compares with `Object.is`), and the hook's cancellation is sound (`current` guards all three effects, deps change on every selection), so a superseded reply cannot land. This is purely that the page has no way to say "asking".

title: Update stl-thumb integration to generate 8+ camera angles
description: Enhance thumbnail generation to: (1) Use 'stl-thumb --cam-pos x y z' to generate 10 isometric angles maintaining the DEFAULT STYLE: camera at distance ~4.9 from origin, elevation ~24°, same visual perspective as default (2.0, -4.0, 2.0). (2) 10 angles by rotating camera around model: Front-iso (default: 2,-4,2), Back-iso (~-2,4,2), Left-iso (~-4,-2,2), Right-iso (~4,2,2), Top-iso (higher z, maintain angle), Bottom-iso (lower z), plus 4 diagonal corners (NE, NW, SE, SW at ~4,±2,2 variants). FOV auto-adjusts. (3) Combine all 10 into SPRITE SHEET PNG using PIL/Pillow (5x2 grid). (4) Store camera coords and grid metadata. Generate during file scan.

Implemented create_sprite_sheet() with 10 isometric camera angles (6 primary + 4 diagonal), PIL/Pillow integration for sprite combining (2x5 grid, 512x512 tiles), and sprite_metadata generation. Added Pillow==11.1.0 to requirements. All 319 tests passing.

title: [guides] Texture blurb counts are hand-written, already wrong in both guides, and cannot be right
description:
Measured 2026-09-29 during review of PR #253 by three reviewers independently, all agreeing.

The texture choices in wall.yaml's floor-texture carry hand-written counts. Every one is wrong against the catalog as it stands:

    stated  actual (all sizes)
    dungeon_stone   71   151
    rough_stone     38    65
    cut-stone       32    77
    towne           23    51
    aztlan          11    24

The wall guide's own wall counts drift the same way: 'Dungeon stone - 121 walls' measures 198. The cause is catalog growth since they were authored, not a predicate change.

WHY CORRECTING THEM DOES NOT FIX IT: the honest number depends on the size already chosen, and texture is asked AFTER size. Dungeon stone is 151 across all sizes, 54 at 2x2 and 18 at 4x4. A single figure in the blurb is wrong in most states the person can actually be in.

WORSE, IN THE WALL GUIDE THE NUMBERS ARE BRANCH-DEPENDENT AND ONE IS A LIVE BUG: on the s2w and wall-on-tile methods the real floor-texture counts are 46/0/20/14/8. Rough stone is ZERO on those branches, so the choice that advertises '38 floors' empties both the floor and floor-base roles and the page renders 'Nothing in the catalog matches this combination yet' - the same failure a patron already hit. That is reachable in production today.

PR #253 dropped the counts from the new floor guide rather than correcting them, keeping only the qualitative claims, which were all verified true. That leaves the two guides inconsistent until wall.yaml is dealt with.

THE FIX WORTH BUILDING: derive them. The engine already returns a count per answer for from_combination refinements (the base-clips question shows them), so the machinery exists; from_namespace choices do not get one. Deriving would make the number correct per branch and per size, and would delete a whole class of prose that goes stale silently.

Failing that, remove them from wall.yaml too.

CORRECTION 2026-09-30, measured against production after the full fixture import. The paragraph above says rough stone is zero on s2w and wall-on-tile and therefore empties both roles live on openforge.tools. THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Sweeping rough stone across all 3 methods x 8 sizes in production gives exactly one dead cell, separate-wall at 1x1, which is the all-texture case in openforge_catalog-f8l and nothing to do with rough stone.

The original measurement was taken against a local catalog that was missing base data production has. The counts being wrong is unaffected and is still the substance of this ticket; the claim of a live user-facing failure was wrong and is withdrawn.

Lesson repeated from a-broken-environment-claim-needs-a-control: a failure measured on localhost is a claim about localhost until the same probe is run against the environment being described.

title: [tests] Four incremental-scanner tests fail locally but pass in CI
description:
Found 2026-09-29 while running the full suite for the floor guide. NOT caused by that change: they fail identically with the new fixture moved aside, so the tree equals HEAD.

FAILING (tests/test_incremental.py, class TestIncrementalScanner):
    test_process_existing_file_unchanged
    test_process_existing_file_unchanged_preserves_images
    test_has_changes_for_output_no_changes
    test_tag_comparison_unordered

All four reduce to the same assertion at tests/test_incremental.py:682 and its siblings: scanner._has_changes_for_output(...) returns True where the test expects False — 'assert True is False'. The test feeds the same tags in a different order and expects no change to be detected.

WHY THIS IS ODD AND WORTH LOOKING AT: CI runs the same command, 'pytest tests/ --cov=openforge' (.github/workflows/test.yaml:50), and python-test passed on every commit of PR #251 and on the 0.8.1 release. So these pass there and fail here, which means either the environment differs in a way the test depends on, or CI is not running what it appears to run.

RULED OUT:
- Not the new guide fixture (verified by removing it).
- Not stale bytecode: cleared every __pycache__ under tests/ and openforge/ and they still fail. (Stale .pyc is real here though — tracebacks print paths under /home/devon/MasterworkTools/openforge_catalog, an older checkout name, which is confusing when reading a failure.)
- Not a local-file dependency: the sample_files fixture writes its own files into a temp dir.

NOT RULED OUT: python version, --cov changing import behaviour, or DB state (run was PGPORT=5433).

Last touched by 56080b5 'fix: prevent duplicate deprecated entries in incremental scanner'.

WHY IT MATTERS: a suite that fails on a developer machine and passes in CI trains people to ignore local failures, which is how a real one gets through. Worth resolving either way — fix the tests, or find out what CI is doing differently.

title: [guides] A pinned part gives no sign it is retired
description:
`/resolve` already carries `deprecated` and `successor_id` on every part's blueprint, and the `GuideBlueprint` type declares neither, so the page cannot tell a live piece from a retired one.

Found in round 13 of PR #241 by silent-failure-hunter, while fixing the larger half: `_pinned_finder` used `get_blueprint_by_md5`, the one md5 lookup in the app that does not skip a retired row, so a pin from an aged shared link was served the superseded file while the catalog dialog on the same page followed the successor chain and showed its replacement. That is fixed on the PR by switching to `get_current_version_by_md5`.

What remains: a pin whose piece is deprecated with no successor still resolves to that piece. Serving it is deliberate — falling back would cost the person their explicit choice and there is nothing better to show — but the page should say so. It now writes a WARNING, which is the operator's signal, not the reader's.

Needs: `deprecated` (and probably `successor_id`) on `GuideBlueprint`, and something on the part card that reads as 'this file has been retired' without looking like an error.

title: [tags] tag_search pagination is unreliable when blueprint names collide
description: Found during PR #239 round 5. tag_search_blueprints paginates with 'bp2.blueprint_name > (SELECT blueprint_name FROM blueprints WHERE id = next)' — a comparison on blueprint_name alone. 159 names in the catalog are shared by two or more records (mostly bases, e.g. plain#base+curved+radial...), so at a page boundary that lands on a duplicated name the next page can skip or repeat rows. PR #239 added the id as a tiebreaker to both ORDER BY clauses, which makes the ordering total and the LIMIT deterministic, but the pagination predicate still compares only the name, so the keyset is not aligned with the sort key. The fix is a compound comparison — (blueprint_name, id) > (name_of_cursor, id_of_cursor) — which is a change to the paging contract and deserves its own PR. Also worth doing at the same time: test_tag_search_tags and test_tag_search_blueprint_images pass bare tag strings, which _query_tags_include silently drops, so both assert only that a record exists rather than that the search finds it by tag.
notes: Third item, from PR #239 round 7: the DESC arm of the new tiebreaker is never exercised. No test anywhere passes previous= or next= to tag_search_blueprints, so the backwards-paging branch ('ORDER BY blueprint_name DESC, id DESC') never renders — mutating it to 'DESC, ASC' leaves all 127 PR tests green. The effect is a wrong-end tie selection when paging backwards. Whoever fixes the keyset predicate here should add backwards-paging coverage at the same time, because the obvious fix to the WHERE clause will not touch this. Also measured: swapping the two sort keys is now caught, but only since the ordering tests grew mixed names — with a single name a sort has nothing to do and can return its input untouched.

title: [guides] Wall texture should drive the floor texture default, as config rather than hand-written clauses
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30: 'while we will be making wall and floor textures data driven, we want wall textures to change the default for floor textures when they are selected, and in some cases that means we need some config for recommending a specific floor texture to go with a wall texture (we see this in towne).'

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS HAND-WRITTEN. wall.yaml's floor-texture refinement carries a branching default - a list of clauses, first match wins:

    when texture is towne or stone_brick  -> texture|towne
    otherwise                             -> texture|dungeon_stone

So a towne wall already recommends a wood floor, and a stone_brick wall does too, which is the case Devon names. The schema calls this a 'recommendation' and explicitly supports reading earlier answers.

THE GAP, measured against production 2026-09-30. Two textures have floors of their own and are not mapped, so they fall through to the dungeon stone clause:

    wall texture     recommends floor    floor it picks
    dungeon_stone -> dungeon_stone       dungeon_stone%block#floor.2x2.openforge.stl
    towne         -> towne               towne%long_planks#floor.2x2.openforge.stl
    stone_brick   -> towne               towne%long_planks#floor.2x2.openforge.stl
    nova_trail    -> dungeon_stone       dungeon_stone%block#floor.2x2.openforge.stl
    aztlan        -> dungeon_stone       dungeon_stone%block#floor.2x2.openforge.stl

A Nova Trail wall on a dungeon stone floor is a defensible build but almost certainly not the one to recommend, and nobody chose it - it is what the fallback does.

WHY THIS BLOCKS ON THE DATA-DRIVEN WORK, and why it is not just 'add two more clauses'. openforge_catalog-g1g makes the texture list derive from the catalog. A derived list cannot be paired with a hand-enumerated set of when-clauses: the whole point is that a scanned texture appears without a fixture edit, and under the current shape it would appear in the list and silently recommend a dungeon stone floor. The mapping has to become data alongside the list.

THE ALGORITHM, from Devon 2026-09-30. Config is an OVERRIDE for the exceptions, not an exhaustive map. Three steps, each conditional on a matching floor existing:

  1. check config. If it recommends a floor texture for this wall texture, use that - if it exists.
  2. otherwise recommend the SAME TOP LEVEL texture - if it exists.
  3. otherwise recommend dungeon stone block.

Two things this gets right that an enumerated map does not. A newly scanned texture needs no config at all: step 2 pairs it with itself the moment it has floors, which is what makes this compatible with deriving the list (openforge_catalog-g1g). And config shrinks to the cases that are genuinely design decisions - today that is towne and stone_brick, where a stone_brick wall wants a towne floor, which no tag can derive.

Note each step is a resolution and not just a lookup: 'use that if it exists' means checking the catalog for a floor in that texture under the rest of the current build, and falling through when there is none. A wall texture with no floors at all - necro, whose own blurb says 'no matching floor' - falls to step 3 by that rule rather than needing an entry.

Note also that step 3 is dungeon stone BLOCK specifically, texture|dungeon_stone|block, which is narrower than the current fallback of texture|dungeon_stone. Today the difference is invisible because the floor role's prefer list puts block first, so it wins anyway; stating it as block makes the recommendation independent of that ordering.

CONFIRMED WHILE INVESTIGATING, so nobody wonders whether bases need the same treatment: floor bases are ALWAYS plain. All 324 shape|base|square carry texture|plain, including all 95 build|s2w ones. That is why the texture refinement already excludes floor-base, and it means this ticket is only about the floor's own texture, not about anything under it.

title: No test exercises the pooled DB path, so a pool-return regression is invisible
description:
Found by resource-leak-reviewer in round 8 of PR #241, pre-existing.

ensure_app_initialized (openforge/app/index.py:32-44) runs on before_request and REBUILDS app.db, and init_app sets use_pool = not app.config["TESTING"]. So the pytest suites never exercise the pooled path at all -- every test request opens and closes a raw psycopg.connect.

Consequence: no test in this repo can catch a pool-return regression. A connection that is borrowed and not returned, or returned broken, is invisible to CI.

The reviewer's own first probe was silently measuring the non-pooled path; the real numbers came from pinning app._initialized = True and asserting the pooled connection is NOT closed at request end, to prove the pooled db had survived.

Worth fixing because this PR's risk profile is connection-shaped: it adds an endpoint that issues ~50 statements per request and a new unhandled-exception path that unwinds through two `with` blocks. Both were verified by hand in round 8 (601 borrows, pool_available back to full, zero idle-in-transaction) -- but nothing stops the next change regressing it.

title: [guides] Dual/triplex wall bases can never be offered, and per-face connectors aren't modelled
description:
Devon, 2026-09-30: 'there are some options for bases when it's s2w that aren't available, so that needs to be more data driven as well (specifically, there are bases with options where the part of the base facing the wall is triplex (openlock, 3 clip holes on the side, no magnets) where the other 3 faces have openlock and magnetic. this is intended to pair with walls that don't use magnets, while still offering magnets on floor joints).'

MEASURED against production 2026-09-30.

WHAT EXISTS. 41 bases carry connection|dual. Every one of them is shape|base|wall, build|separate wall, and texture|plain. Filenames carry the real story - plain#base+wall.A+dual.openlock,magnetic+flex.stl, plain#base+wall.A+dual.openlock+topless.stl and so on - where '+dual' marks the mixed arrangement and the suffix lists the connectors present somewhere on the part.

WHY THEY ARE UNREACHABLE TODAY. The wall guide's texture refinement is role '*' with except_roles [floor-base, floor], so it constrains wall-base. All 41 dual bases are texture|plain, and there are zero dual bases in any other texture:

    shape|base + connection|dual                        41
    shape|base + connection|dual + texture|dungeon_stone 0
    shape|base + connection|dual + texture|plain        41

The refinement's substitute map handles three cases - towne -> wood, stone_brick and mortar_and_stone -> foundation, all for wall-base - but nothing maps to plain. So whichever texture a person picks, the dual bases are filtered out, and connection|dual never appears as an answer in base-clips even though it is in the connection namespace and is not in that question's exclude list.

THE DEEPER PROBLEM, which is the part that needs modelling rather than a substitute entry. The connectors on these parts are PER FACE: the wall-facing side is triplex - OpenLOCK, three clip holes, no magnets - and the other three faces are OpenLOCK and magnetic. The tag vocabulary is per part, so connection|dual says 'this base mixes two schemes' without saying which face has which. A question asking 'how do the bases clip together' cannot express 'magnets on the floor joints, none toward the wall', because the answer it derives is a set of connectors for the whole piece.

That is exactly the arrangement Devon describes as intended: pair with walls that do not use magnets, while still offering magnets on the floor joints. It is a real build choice the catalog supports and the guide cannot currently ask about.

ALSO OBSERVED, probably correct and noted so nobody chases it. s2w and separate-wall offer 7 clip answers where wall-on-tile offers 9, missing the two unsupported variants. That looks like the intersection working as designed: on those methods base-clips applies to both floor-base and wall-base and offers only answers both can satisfy, and unsupported wall bases exist (40 separate-wall, 12 s2w) but not in every texture and size. Worth confirming rather than assuming when this is picked up.

RELATED. openforge_catalog-g1g is the same shape of problem for textures - a hand-curated list where the catalog should drive it. This one is harder: textures need the list derived, this needs the underlying facts recorded before anything can derive them.

title: [guided builds] Author the floor guide
description:
A second guide, keyed 'floor': the floor half of the wall guide standing on its own, for someone laying a room or hallway floor rather than building a wall.

Requested by Devon 2026-09-29. Bead filed after the work rather than before, which is the wrong way round.

SHAPE: two steps (floor-print, size), two roles (floor, floor-base), three refinements (texture, base-clips, floor-clips). Deliberately the same PROSE as the wall guide's floor half, so the two read as one voice. The PREDICATES are not identical, and the differences are the substance of the review below - an earlier version of this line claimed they were, which is the same retracted claim the CORRECTED paragraph deals with.

CORRECTED 2026-09-29 (round 2 of PR #253). This ticket originally said: "The ONE predicate that differs, and on purpose: the wall guide's floor role carries allow: [component|wall], because the floor it picks may be a tile with a wall standing on it. The floor guide leaves that out, so deny_children: [component] sweeps component|wall away." THAT IS WRONG and would otherwise have been filed as this ticket's permanent record.

Measurement: the two queries select the IDENTICAL 533 pieces. Only 14 catalog pieces carry both shape|floor and component|wall, and all 14 also carry shape|floor|wall|angled or shape|floor|s2w, so the shape sweep refuses them whether or not the component term is present. The wall guide needs that allow only because its method options require shape|floor|wall, which exempts the tag from the sweep and lets the component term bite. No option in the floor guide does that.

WHAT ACTUALLY DIFFERS, after review: the floor role drops two inert terms (allow: [component|wall] and deny: [shape|base]), and - the one that is not cosmetic - the with-base option requires connection|openforge where the wall guide constrains nothing. Without it the browse dialog offers one-piece OpenLOCK tiles, which already are bases, under a separate base. 128 of 313 otherwise-reachable floors. The wall guide still has that hole: openforge_catalog-39q.

ROLE ACTIVATION: roles come only from chosen step options (_roles_in_play iterates the option's roles KEYS, so a key mapped to null still puts the role in play). The wall guide's 'method' step does that job there; with no method question here, floor-print introduces both roles.

CORRECTED 2026-09-29 (round 4): this paragraph previously said floor-print introduces 'floor' with a null predicate, taking no constraint from the answer. That was true of the first version of the fixture and stopped being true in round 1, which swapped them. As shipped, floor-BASE is the null one - its role query already requires shape|base|square - while 'floor' is constrained in both options, and on with-base that constraint (connection|openforge) is the whole point of the fix. Read uncorrected, this said with-base puts nothing on the floor, which is the -39q defect this ticket's own work closes. Third copy of the same retracted claim; the other two were fixed in round 3.

ORDERING: floor sorts before wall because get_all_guides is ORDER BY guide_key and 'floor' < 'wall'. That satisfies the requirement by alphabet, not by declaration. A third guide lands wherever its key sorts. If the order ever needs to be authored rather than inferred, that is a column and a fixture field, and is not built.

VERIFIED, final figures: 80 of 80 size x print x texture combinations resolve with no empty role, and every with-base floor carries connection|openforge. A reviewer separately ran 360 resolves (8 sizes x 5 textures x 9 clip combinations) with zero footprint mismatches, and re-ran the engine against the pre-review document for 0 of 80 recommendations differing. Defaults resolve to dungeon_stone block 2x2 floor plus the plain 2x2 openlock+topless,magnetic+flex base. No console errors on the entry page or the guide page.
